title.zh: 卷二百八十二 列傳第四十一 李沆 王旦 向敏中
title.en: Volume 282 Biographies 41: Li Hang, Wang Dan, Xiang Minzhong
title.raw: 卷二百八十二 列傳第四十一 李沆 王旦 向敏中 Volume 282 Biographies 41: Li Hang, Wang Dan, Xiang Minzhong

sentences.zh: 李沆，字太初，洺州肥鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Hang, courtesy name Taichu, was a man of Feixiang in Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang, styled Taichu, came from Feixiang in Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖豐，泰陵令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Feng was magistrate of Tailin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Feng had served as magistrate of Tailin.

sentences.zh: 祖滔，洺州團練判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tao was regimental training commissioner judge of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao had been regimental training commissioner judge at Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 父炳，從邢帥薛懷讓辟，為觀察支使。

translations.literal: His father Bing, following Xing's military commissioner Xue Huairang, was summoned and served as administrative aide to the observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bing entered service under Xing's military commissioner Xue Huairang as administrative aide to the observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 懷讓徙同州，又為掌書記，歷邠州、鳳翔判官，拜殿中侍御史、知舒州。

translations.literal: When Huairang was transferred to Tongzhou, Bing again served as chief secretary; he successively held posts as judge at Binzhou and Fengxiang, was appointed Attendant Censor within the Palace and prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huairang moved to Tongzhou, Bing again served as chief secretary, later held judgeships at Binzhou and Fengxiang, and was appointed Attendant Censor within the Palace and prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖征金陵，緣淮供億，惟舒尤甚，以勞加侍御史，卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu campaigned against Jinling, supplies were provisioned along the Huai; Shuzhou bore the heaviest burden. For his labors he was promoted to Attendant Censor and then died.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu's campaign against Jinling, provisioning ran along the Huai River, and Shuzhou bore the heaviest load. Bing was promoted to Attendant Censor for his exertions, then died.

sentences.zh: 沆少好學，器度宏遠，炳嘗語人曰：「此兒異日必至公輔。」

translations.literal: Hang from youth loved learning and his bearing was broad and far-reaching. Bing once told others, "This boy will surely reach the rank of chief minister one day."
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hang loved learning, and his temperament was large and far-seeing. Bing once told acquaintances, "This son will one day reach the highest offices of state."

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，舉進士甲科，為將作監丞、通判潭州，遷右贊善大夫，轉著作郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination in the first class, was made Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and vice-prefect of Tanzhou, was promoted to Right Assistant for Goodness Grandee, and transferred to Drafting Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he took the jinshi in the top class, became Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and vice-prefect of Tanzhou, was promoted to Right Assistant for Goodness Grandee, and then moved to Drafting Archivist.

sentences.zh: 相府召試約束邊將詔書，既奏御，太宗甚悅，命直史館。

translations.literal: The chief council's office summoned him to draft an edict restraining frontier generals; after it was submitted to the throne, Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and appointed him attendant of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The chief council summoned him to draft an edict restraining frontier generals. When it reached the throne, Emperor Taizong was delighted and made him attendant of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，右拾遺王化基上書自薦，太宗謂宰相曰：「李沆、宋湜，皆嘉士也。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Right Remonstrance Recipient Wang Huaji submitted a memorial recommending himself. Emperor Taizong told the chief councilors, "Li Hang and Song Shi are both fine men."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, Right Remonstrance Recipient Wang Huaji memorialized recommending himself. Emperor Taizong told the chief councilors, "Li Hang and Song Shi are both worthy men."

sentences.zh: 即命中書並化基召試，並除右補闕、知制誥。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the Secretariat to summon Huaji together with them for examination, and all three were appointed Right Supplementary Censors and Drafting Recipients.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Secretariat to examine Huaji together with them, and all three were appointed Right Supplementary Censors and Drafting Recipients.

sentences.zh: 沆位最下，特升於上，各賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: Hang ranked lowest, yet was specially placed above the others; each was granted a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hang ranked last, he was specially placed above the others, and each man received a grant of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 又以沆素貧，多負人錢，別賜三十萬償之。

translations.literal: Because Hang had long been poor and owed much money to others, he was separately granted three hundred thousand to repay his debts.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hang had long been poor and deeply in debt, the court separately granted him three hundred thousand cash to settle what he owed.

sentences.zh: 四年，與翰林學士宋白同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served with Hanlin Academician Song Bai as co-examiner for the civil service examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he and Hanlin Academician Song Bai jointly supervised the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 謗議雖眾，而不歸咎於沆。

translations.literal: Though criticism was widespread, blame was not laid on Hang.
translations.idiomatic: Though criticism ran wide, none of it was laid at Hang's door.

sentences.zh: 遷職方員外郎，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outer Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel and summoned into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Outer Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel and summoned into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he directed the Ministry of Personnel's selection office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he took charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection office.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍曲宴，太宗目送之曰：「李沆風度端凝，真貴人也。」

translations.literal: Once, while attending an informal banquet, Emperor Taizong watched him depart and said, "Li Hang's bearing is dignified and composed—a truly noble man."
translations.idiomatic: Once, after an informal banquet, Emperor Taizong watched him leave and said, "Li Hang's bearing is grave and steady—a man of true nobility."

sentences.zh: 三年，拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Attendant Censor and participation councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Attendant Censor and participation councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，以本官罷，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was dismissed from his post and made a court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he left office and became a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁內艱，起復，遂出知昇州。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother, was recalled before the mourning period ended, and was then sent out as prefect of Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he entered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning before the period ended, and was appointed prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改知河南府。

translations.literal: Before he departed, his appointment was changed to prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the appointment was changed to prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗升儲，遷禮部侍郎兼太子賓客，詔東宮待以師傅禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong was established as heir apparent, Hang was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Court Gentleman Consultant to the Heir Apparent; an edict ordered that the Eastern Palace treat him with the rites due a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong was made heir apparent, Hang was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Court Gentleman Consultant to the Heir Apparent, with orders that the Eastern Palace receive him with a tutor's honors.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷戶部侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded to the throne, Hang was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and participation councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Hang became Vice Minister of Revenue and participation councilor.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，以本官平章事，監修國史，改中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was made chief councilor in his existing rank, supervised compilation of the national history, and was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping era he was made chief councilor at his existing rank, put in charge of compiling the national history, and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會契丹犯邊，真宗北幸，命沆留守，京師肅然。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the frontier, Emperor Zhenzong went north in person; Hang was ordered to remain behind as regent, and the capital became orderly and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan struck the frontier, Zhenzong marched north in person and left Hang as regent in the capital, which remained calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 真宗還，沆迎於郊，命坐置酒，慰勞久之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong returned, Hang met him in the suburbs; the emperor had him seated and wine set out, and comforted him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong returned, Hang met him outside the city; the emperor had him sit, poured wine, and long thanked him for his service.

sentences.zh: 累加門下侍郎、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was in time promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 真宗問治道所宜先，沆曰：「不用浮薄新進喜事之人，此最為先。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong asked what should come first in the way of governance. Hang said, "Do not employ frivolous newly advanced men eager for novelty—this should come first."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong asked what ought to come first in governing the realm, Hang answered, "Above all, do not employ shallow newcomers hungry for novelty."

sentences.zh: 問其人，曰：「如梅詢、曾致堯等是矣。」

translations.literal: Asked who such men were, he said, "Men like Mei Xun and Zeng Zhiyao are examples."
translations.idiomatic: Asked who he meant, he said, "Men like Mei Xun and Zeng Zhiyao, for instance."

sentences.zh: 後致堯副溫仲舒安撫陝西，於閣門疏言仲舒不足與共事，輕銳之黨無不稱快，沆不喜也，因用他人副仲舒，罷致堯。

translations.literal: Later Zeng Zhiyao served as deputy to Wen Zhongshu on the Shaanxi pacification commission and submitted a memorial at the Gate of Virtuous Proclamation saying that Zhongshu was unfit to work with; the faction of the rash and ambitious all rejoiced. Hang was displeased, and so another man was used as Zhongshu's deputy and Zhiyao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zeng Zhiyao served as Wen Zhongshu's deputy on the Shaanxi pacification commission, he memorialized at the palace gate that Zhongshu was unfit to serve with. The hotheaded faction cheered, but Hang was displeased; he replaced Zhiyao with another deputy and removed Zhiyao from office.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語及唐人樹黨難制，遂使王室微弱，蓋奸邪難辨爾，沆對曰：「佞言似忠，奸言似信，至如盧杞蒙蔽德宗，李勉以為真奸邪是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke of how Tang men formed factions that were hard to control and thereby weakened the royal house—surely because the wicked are hard to distinguish. Hang replied, "Flattering words seem loyal, and treacherous words seem trustworthy. Lu Qi deceived Emperor Dezong of Tang, yet Li Mian recognized him as truly wicked—that is the sort of case I mean."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once remarked that Tang officials had formed factions hard to break up, weakening the throne—because wicked men are so difficult to tell apart. Hang replied, "Flattery sounds loyal, and treachery sounds sincere. Lu Qi blinded Emperor Dezong, yet Li Mian saw through him as a true villain—that is what I mean."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「奸邪之跡，雖曰難辨，然久之自敗。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said, "The traces of the wicked, though said to be hard to distinguish, in time expose themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "Wicked men may be hard to spot at first, but in time they undo themselves."

sentences.zh: 一夕，遣使持手詔欲以劉氏為貴妃，沆對使者引燭焚詔，附奏曰：「但道臣沆以為不可。」

translations.literal: One evening an envoy arrived bearing an autograph edict seeking to make Lady Liu an imperial consort. Hang, facing the envoy, lit a candle and burned the edict, and appended a memorial saying, "Simply report that your subject Hang considers it inadvisable."
translations.idiomatic: One night an envoy arrived with an autograph edict to elevate Lady Liu to imperial consort. Hang took the edict from the envoy, lit a candle, and burned it, adding in his memorial, "Simply say that your subject Hang holds this inadvisable."

sentences.zh: 其議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉石保吉求為使相，復問沆，沆曰：「賞典之行，須有所自。

translations.literal: Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Shi Baoji sought to become a commissioner with chief councilor status. The emperor again asked Hang, who said, "The bestowal of honors must have its grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Shi Baoji sought appointment as a commissioner with chief councilor rank. The emperor again consulted Hang, who said, "Honors must rest on some merit.

sentences.zh: 保吉因緣戚里，無攻戰之勞，臺席之拜，恐騰物議。」

translations.literal: Baoji relies on imperial kinship and has no merit from attack or battle; to grant him a seat at the chief council would, I fear, stir public criticism."
translations.idiomatic: Baoji owes his standing to imperial kinship alone and has no record of battlefield service. To seat him at the chief council would, I fear, provoke widespread criticism."

sentences.zh: 他日再三問之，執議如初，遂止。

translations.literal: On later days the emperor asked again and again; Hang held to his view as before, and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On later occasions the emperor asked again and again, but Hang held firm, and the appointment was blocked.

sentences.zh: 帝以沆無密奏，謂之曰：「人皆有密啟，卿獨無，何也？」

translations.literal: Because Hang submitted no secret memorials, the emperor said to him, "Everyone else has secret reports; you alone have none. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Noting that Hang never filed secret memorials, the emperor asked him, "Every man has secret reports; you alone have none. Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣待罪宰相，公事則公言之，何用密啟？

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject serves in the chief council bearing blame; public affairs should be spoken of publicly—what need is there for secret reports?
translations.idiomatic: Hang answered, "I serve as chief councilor under blame; public business should be spoken of in public—what use are secret reports?

sentences.zh: 夫人臣有密啟者，非讒即佞，臣常惡之，豈可效尤？」

translations.literal: When a minister has secret reports, they are either slander or flattery. I have always detested that—how could I imitate it?"
translations.idiomatic: When a minister keeps secret reports, they are either slander or flattery. I have always loathed that practice—why should I copy it?"

sentences.zh: 時李繼遷久叛，兵眾日盛，有圖取朔方之意。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jichong had long been in rebellion; his forces grew daily stronger, and he intended to seize Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jichong had long been in rebellion, his forces were swelling, and he meant to seize Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷困於飛輓，中外咸以為靈州乃必爭之地，苟失之，則緣邊諸郡皆不可保。

translations.literal: The court was strained by urgent transport, and inside and outside the government alike held that Lingzhou was ground that must be contested; if it were lost, none of the frontier prefectures could be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The court was exhausted by urgent supply convoys, and officials everywhere agreed that Lingzhou was ground that had to be held; lose it, and the frontier prefectures could not be kept.

sentences.zh: 帝頗惑之，因訪於沆，沆曰：「繼遷不死，靈州非朝廷有也。

translations.literal: The emperor was much perplexed and therefore sought Hang's view. Hang said, "So long as Jichong lives, Lingzhou will not belong to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply uncertain and asked Hang's view. Hang said, "While Jichong lives, Lingzhou will not remain the court's.

sentences.zh: 莫若遣使密召州將，使部分軍民空壘而歸，如此，則關右之民息肩矣。」

translations.literal: Better to send an envoy in secret to summon the prefect, have him lead the army and people to abandon the fortress and return. In that way the people of the western passes would be relieved of their burden."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send a secret envoy to summon the prefect, have him evacuate the garrison with army and people, and withdraw. Then the people of the western passes could at last set down their loads."

sentences.zh: 方眾議各異，未即從沆言，未幾而靈州陷，帝由是益重之。

translations.literal: While the various opinions still differed and the court did not immediately follow Hang's advice, before long Lingzhou fell, and the emperor therefore valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion was still divided and the court did not immediately follow him, but before long Lingzhou fell, and the emperor thereafter esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 沆為相，王旦參政事，以西北用兵，或至旰食。

translations.literal: While Hang served as chief councilor, Wang Dan served as participation councilor; because of warfare in the northwest, they sometimes did not finish their meals until sunset.
translations.idiomatic: While Hang was chief councilor and Wang Dan participation councilor, northwestern warfare sometimes kept them at their desks until sunset.

sentences.zh: 旦歎曰：「我輩安能坐致太平，得優遊無事耶？」

translations.literal: Dan sighed and said, "How can we sit here and bring about great peace, enjoying leisure with nothing to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan sighed and said, "How can we sit here and bring about great peace, enjoying ease with nothing to do?"

sentences.zh: 沆曰：「少有憂勤，足為警戒。

translations.literal: Hang said, "A little worry and diligence is enough to serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hang said, "A little worry and hard work is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 他日四方寧謐，朝廷未必無事。」

translations.literal: Another day, when the four quarters are calm and quiet, the court will not necessarily be free of trouble."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is calm, the court may still not be free of trouble."

sentences.zh: 後契丹和親，旦問何如，沆曰：「善則善矣，然邊患既息，恐人主漸生侈心耳。」

translations.literal: Later, when the Khitan made peace through marriage alliance, Dan asked what Hang thought. Hang said, "It is good, to be sure—but once the frontier trouble has ceased, I fear the sovereign will gradually grow extravagant."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Khitan made peace by marriage alliance, Dan asked Hang's view. Hang said, "It is well enough—but once the frontier is quiet, I fear the emperor will slowly turn to extravagance."

sentences.zh: 旦未以為然。

translations.literal: Dan did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Dan did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 沆又日取四方水旱盜賊奏之，旦以為細事不足煩上聽。

translations.literal: Hang also daily took memorials on floods, drought, banditry, and theft from the four quarters. Dan thought such small matters were not worth troubling the emperor to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Hang also daily brought the emperor memorials on flood, drought, banditry, and theft from every quarter. Dan thought such small matters were not worth the emperor's ear.

sentences.zh: 沆曰：「人主少年，當使知四方艱難。

translations.literal: Hang said, "The sovereign is still young; he should be made to know the hardships of the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Hang said, "The emperor is still young; he ought to know how hard life is across the realm.

sentences.zh: 不然，血氣方剛，不留意聲色犬馬，則土木、甲兵、禱祠之事作矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, while his blood and vigor are at their height, if he pays no heed to music, color, dogs, and horses, then matters of earthworks, armor, and prayer will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, in the flush of youth, if he pays no heed to music, women, hunting dogs, and horses, he will turn to palaces, armor, and lavish rites.

sentences.zh: 吾老，不及見此，此參政他日之憂也。」

translations.literal: I am old and will not live to see it, but this will be the participation councilor's worry hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: I am old and will not live to see it—but that will be your worry as participation councilor."

sentences.zh: 沆沒後，真宗以契丹既和，西夏納款，遂封岱祠汾，大營宮觀，蒐講墜典，靡有暇日。

translations.literal: After Hang's death, Emperor Zhenzong, because the Khitan had made peace and Western Xia had submitted tribute, then performed the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai, sacrificed at the Fen River, built great palaces and temples on a vast scale, and searched out and restored fallen rites, with scarcely a free day.
translations.idiomatic: After Hang died, Zhenzong—with the Khitan at peace and Western Xia paying tribute—went on to the feng and shan at Mount Tai, sacrifice at the Fen River, grand palace and temple building, and the revival of neglected rites, with scarcely a day to spare.

sentences.zh: 旦親見王欽若、丁謂等所為，欲諫則業已同之，欲去則上遇之厚，乃以沆先識之遠，歎曰：「李文靖真聖人也。」

translations.literal: Dan personally witnessed what Wang Qinruo, Ding Wei, and others were doing; he wished to remonstrate but had already gone along with them, and wished to withdraw but was treated generously by the emperor. He therefore sighed at Hang's foresight and said, "Li Wenjing was truly a sage."
translations.idiomatic: Dan saw for himself what Wang Qinruo, Ding Wei, and the rest were doing. He wanted to remonstrate but had already joined them; he wanted to leave but was too well treated by the emperor. He sighed at Hang's foresight and said, "Li Wenjing was a true sage."

sentences.zh: 當時遂謂之「聖相」。

translations.literal: At the time people therefore called him the "sage chief councilor."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him the "sage chief councilor."

sentences.zh: 寇準與丁謂善，屢以謂才薦於沆，不用。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was on good terms with Ding Wei and repeatedly recommended Wei's talent to Hang, but Hang would not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was friendly with Ding Wei and repeatedly commended Wei's talent to Hang, but Hang would not use him.

sentences.zh: 準問之，沆曰：「顧其為人，可使之在人上乎？」

translations.literal: Zhun asked why. Hang said, "Considering the sort of man he is, could one allow him to stand above others?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhun asked why. Hang said, "Given the sort of man he is, could you put him above others?"

sentences.zh: 準曰：「如謂者，相公終能抑之使在人下乎？」

translations.literal: Zhun said, "If a man like Wei is employed, can the chief councilor ultimately keep him beneath others?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhun said, "Once a man like Wei is in office, can even the chief councilor keep him beneath others?"

sentences.zh: 沆笑曰：「他日後悔，當思吾言也。」

translations.literal: Hang smiled and said, "When you regret it later, you will remember my words."
translations.idiomatic: Hang smiled and said, "When you regret it later, you will remember what I said."

sentences.zh: 準後為謂所傾，始伏沆言。

translations.literal: Later Zhun was overthrown by Wei and at last acknowledged the truth of Hang's words.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhun was ruined by Wei and at last conceded that Hang had been right.

sentences.zh: 沆為相，接賓客，常寡言。

translations.literal: While Hang served as chief councilor and received guests, he was usually sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: As chief councilor, Hang received guests but usually said little.

sentences.zh: 馬亮與沆同年生，又與其弟維善，語維曰：「外議以大兄為無口匏。」

translations.literal: Ma Liang was born in the same year as Hang and was also on good terms with his younger brother Wei. He said to Wei, "Outside opinion holds that your elder brother is a speechless gourd."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang was Hang's year-mate and a friend of his younger brother Wei. He told Wei, "People outside say your elder brother is a mute gourd."

sentences.zh: 維乘間達亮語，沆曰：「吾非不知也。

translations.literal: Wei seized an opportunity to relay Liang's remark. Hang said, "It is not that I do not know.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed Liang's remark along when he could. Hang said, "It is not that I do not know.

sentences.zh: 然今之朝士得升殿言事，上封論奏，了無壅蔽，多下有司，皆見之矣。

translations.literal: But today court gentlemen who ascend the hall to speak on affairs, submit sealed memorials, and discuss policy meet with no obstruction at all; most matters are sent down to the relevant offices, and all can see that.
translations.idiomatic: But today any court gentleman may speak in hall audience, submit sealed memorials, and debate policy without obstruction; most matters go down to the offices below, and all can see that.

sentences.zh: 若邦國大事，北有契丹，西有夏人，日旰條議所以備禦之策，非不詳究。

translations.literal: If it is a matter of state, the Khitan lie to the north and the Xia people to the west; until sunset we itemize plans for defense—and we do not fail to examine them closely.
translations.idiomatic: On matters of state, the Khitan threaten the north and the Xia the west; until sunset we go through plans for defense in detail—and we leave nothing unexamined.

sentences.zh: 薦紳如李宗諤、趙安仁，皆時之英秀，與之談，猶不能啟發吾意。

translations.literal: Among the gentry, men like Li Zong'e and Zhao Anren are outstanding talents of the age; talk with them, and still they cannot stir my thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Among officials, men like Li Zong'e and Zhao Anren are the finest of the age, yet even talking with them does not stir my thinking.

sentences.zh: 自餘通籍之子，坐起拜揖，尚周章失次，即席必自論功最，以希寵獎，此有何策而與之接語哉？

translations.literal: As for the rest of those entered on the registers, in rising, sitting, bowing, and yielding they are still flustered and out of order; once seated they invariably speak of their own achievements, hoping for favor and reward—what policy is there to discuss with such men?
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the registry men can barely manage to rise, sit, bow, and yield without confusion; once seated they always recount their own achievements hoping for favor—what policy is there to discuss with them?

sentences.zh: 苟屈意妄言，即世所謂籠罩。

translations.literal: If one humors them and speaks recklessly, that is what the world calls "drawing the cage over them."
translations.idiomatic: To humor them and talk nonsense is what the world calls "drawing the cage over them."

sentences.zh: 籠罩之事，僕病未能也。」

translations.literal: As for drawing the cage over people, your servant is too ill for that."
translations.idiomatic: As for that sort of flattery, I am too sick at heart to manage it."

sentences.zh: 沆又嘗言：「居重位實無補，惟中外所陳利害，一切報罷之，此少以報國爾。

translations.literal: Hang also once said, "Holding high office in truth adds nothing; only in rejecting every benefit and harm reported from inside and outside the government is there a little repayment to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hang also said, "High office in truth accomplishes little; my small service to the state is to reject every proposal of benefit and harm reported from within and without.

sentences.zh: 朝廷防製，纖悉備具，或徇所陳請，施行一事，即所傷多矣，陸象先曰『庸人擾之』是已。

translations.literal: The court's safeguards are minute and complete; if one indulges what is requested and carries out a single measure, the harm done is great—Lu Xiangxian's words, "Meddling by mediocre men," apply here.
translations.idiomatic: The court's safeguards are exhaustive; indulge one petition and implement one measure, and the harm is great—Lu Xiangxian's "meddling by mediocre men" says it.

sentences.zh: 憸人苟一時之進，豈念厲民耶？」

translations.literal: Wicked men, if they can advance for a moment, how would they consider harm to the people?"
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men seeking a moment's advancement never think of the people's suffering."

sentences.zh: 沆為相，常讀《論語》，或問之，沆曰：「沆為宰相，如《論語》中『節用而愛人，使民以時』，尚未能行。

translations.literal: While Hang served as chief councilor he often read the Analects. When asked about it, Hang said, "Hang as chief councilor—for the Analects' "Be sparing in expenditure and love the people, and employ the people at the proper seasons," I have not yet been able to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: As chief councilor Hang often read the Analects. When asked why, he said, "As chief councilor, even the Analects' "Be sparing in expenditure and love the people; employ the people at the proper seasons"—I have not yet managed to live by that.

sentences.zh: 聖人之言，終身誦之可也。」

translations.literal: The sage's words may be recited all one's life."
translations.idiomatic: The sage's words are worth reciting all one's life."

sentences.zh: 景德元年七月，沆待漏將朝，疾作而歸，詔太醫診視，撫問之使相望於道。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Jingde, Hang was waiting at the dawn audience when illness came upon him and he returned home. An edict ordered the imperial physicians to examine him, and envoys sent to inquire after him followed one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Jingde, Hang was waiting for dawn audience when he fell ill and went home. The court sent imperial physicians and a stream of envoys to inquire after him along the road.

sentences.zh: 明日，駕往臨問，賜白金五千兩。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor went in person to inquire after him and granted five thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor came in person to visit him and granted five thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 方還宮而沆薨，年五十八。

translations.literal: Just as the emperor was returning to the palace, Hang died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the emperor was returning to the palace, Hang died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上聞之驚歎，趣駕再往，臨哭之慟，謂左右曰：「沆為大臣，忠良純厚，始終如一，豈意不享遐壽！」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard it he was startled and sighed; he hastened his carriage to go again and wept bitterly at the bier, saying to those beside him, "Hang was a great minister—loyal, good, pure, and thick from first to last. Who would have thought he would not enjoy long life!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was shocked and grieved; he hurried back and wept bitterly over the body, telling those beside him, "Hang was a great minister—loyal, upright, and steadfast to the end. Who would have thought he would not live to old age!"

sentences.zh: 言終又泣下。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he wept again.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he wept again.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，贈太尉、中書令，諡文靖。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for five days. He was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for five days. Hang was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 錄其弟國子博士贄為虞部員外郎、光祿寺丞源為太子中舍、屯田員外郎直集賢院維為戶部員外郎；

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhi, Doctor of the Directorate of Education, was appointed Outer Bureau Director of the Ministry of Works; Yuan, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Crown Prince Household Attendant; and Wei, Outer Bureau Director of the Agriculture Bureau and attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Outer Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhi, a doctor of the Directorate of Education, was made Outer Bureau Director of the Ministry of Works; Yuan, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Crown Prince Household Attendant; and Wei, who held the posts of Outer Bureau Director of the Agriculture Bureau and attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was promoted to Outer Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 子宗簡為大理評事；

translations.literal: his son Zongjian was made Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: his son Zongjian was made Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 甥蘇昂、妻兄之子朱濤並同進士出身。

translations.literal: his nephew Su Ang and his wife's brother's son Zhu Tao were both granted jinshi origin.
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Su Ang and his wife's brother's son Zhu Tao were both granted jinshi origin.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，仁宗即位，詔配享真宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, when Emperor Renzong acceded to the throne, an edict ordered that Hang be granted a place in the temple of Emperor Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing, when Renzong took the throne, an edict granted Hang a place in Emperor Zhenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 沆性直諒，內行修謹，言無枝葉，識大體。

translations.literal: Hang's nature was upright and sincere; his private conduct was careful and strict; his speech had no superfluous branches; he grasped the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was upright and candid by nature, careful and strict in private life, spare of speech, and alive to the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 居位慎密，不求聲譽，動遵條製，人莫能干以私。

translations.literal: In office he was cautious and close; he did not seek reputation; in action he followed regulations and systems, and no one could move him by private interest.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was guarded and discreet, sought no fame, and kept to regulation so that no one could sway him by private appeal.

sentences.zh: 公退，終日危坐，未嘗跛倚。

translations.literal: After leaving public business he sat upright all day and never leaned askew.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he sat upright all day and never slouched.

sentences.zh: 治第封丘門內，廳事前僅容旋馬，或言其太隘，沆笑曰：「居第當傳子孫，此為宰相廳事誠隘，為太祝、奉禮廳事已寬矣。」

translations.literal: He built a residence inside the Fengqiu Gate; before the hall there was room only to turn a horse. Some said it was too narrow. Hang smiled and said, "A dwelling should be passed to one's descendants. As a chief councilor's hall it is indeed narrow, but as a hall for a Grand Supplicator or Ceremonial Attendant it is already wide."
translations.idiomatic: He built a house inside the Fengqiu Gate with barely room to turn a horse before the hall. Some said it was too cramped. Hang smiled and said, "A house should pass to one's descendants. For a chief councilor's hall it is tight, but for a Grand Supplicator or Ceremonial Attendant it would be spacious."

sentences.zh: 至於垣頹壁損，不以屑慮。

translations.literal: As for collapsed walls and broken plaster, he gave them no thought.
translations.idiomatic: Collapsed walls and crumbling plaster he did not bother about at all.

sentences.zh: 堂前藥闌壞，妻戒守舍者勿葺以試沆，沆朝夕見之，經月終不言。

translations.literal: The herb fence in front of the hall was broken; his wife warned the housekeeper not to repair it, to test Hang. Hang saw it morning and evening for a month and in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The herb bed in front of the hall fell into ruin; his wife told the caretaker not to repair it, to test Hang. Hang saw it every day for a month and never spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 妻以語沆，沆曰：「豈可以此動吾一念哉！」

translations.literal: His wife told Hang of it. Hang said, "How could such a thing move a thought in me!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife told him. Hang said, "How could that move me!"

sentences.zh: 家人勸治居第，未嘗答，弟維因語次及之，沆曰：「身食厚祿，時有橫賜，計囊裝亦可以治第，但念內典以此世界為缺陷，安得圓滿如意，自求稱足？

translations.literal: The family urged him to repair the residence, but he never answered. His younger brother Wei, in the course of conversation, brought the matter up. Hang said, "I receive a generous salary and from time to time receive special grants; by my reckoning my purse could indeed build a residence. But I reflect that the inner canon treats this world as flawed—how can one achieve perfect fulfillment and ask to be fully satisfied?
translations.idiomatic: The family urged him to rebuild the house, but he never replied. His brother Wei raised it in conversation. Hang said, "I draw a generous salary and receive occasional special grants; by my purse I could build a house. But the sutras call this world flawed—how can one demand perfect satisfaction?

sentences.zh: 今市新宅，須一年繕完，人生朝暮不可保，又豈能久居？

translations.literal: To buy a new residence now would require a year to finish the repairs. Human life from dawn to dusk cannot be assured—how could one dwell in it long?
translations.idiomatic: A new house would take a year to finish. Life from dawn to dusk is uncertain—how long could one live in it?

sentences.zh: 巢林一枝，聊自足耳，安事豐屋哉？」

translations.literal: A single branch in the nest is enough for the moment—what need is there for a grand house?"
translations.idiomatic: One branch in the nest is enough—what need of a palace?"

sentences.zh: 沆與諸弟友愛，尤器重維，暇日相對宴飲清言，未嘗及朝政，亦未嘗問家事。

translations.literal: Hang was affectionate with his younger brothers and especially valued Wei. On free days they faced one another, feasting, drinking, and speaking plainly; he never touched on court affairs, nor ever asked about household matters.
translations.idiomatic: Hang loved his younger brothers and especially esteemed Wei. On free days they feasted and talked at ease, never touching court affairs or household business.

sentences.zh: 沆沒後，或薦梅詢可用，真宗曰：「李沆嘗言其非君子。」

translations.literal: After Hang's death, when someone recommended Mei Xun as usable, Emperor Zhenzong said, "Li Hang once said he was no gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: After Hang died, when someone recommended Mei Xun for office, Emperor Zhenzong said, "Li Hang once said he was no gentleman."

sentences.zh: 其為信倚如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust and reliance placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the trust the emperor placed in his judgment.

sentences.zh: 弟 維

translations.literal: Younger brother: Wei
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Wei

sentences.zh: 維，字仲方，第進士，為保信軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Zhongfang, passed the jinshi examination and served as military commissioner adjutant of the Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Zhongfang, passed the jinshi examination and was appointed adjutant to the military commissioner of the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，獻《聖德詩》，召試中書，擢直集賢院，以沆相，避知歙州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign, he submitted the Ode to Sacred Virtue, was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and promoted to a direct appointment in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; because Li Hang was chancellor, he withdrew from the capital and was made prefect of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenzong's reign he submitted his Ode to Sacred Virtue, was summoned to an examination at the Secretariat, and was promoted to the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Because his brother Li Hang was chancellor, he stepped aside from court and was sent out as prefect of She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至郡，興學舍，歲時行鄉射之禮。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, he established a school and performed the village archery rite at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he founded a school and held the seasonal village archery ceremony each year.

sentences.zh: 沆沒，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: After Li Hang died, he entered the capital as deputy director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Hang's death he returned to the capital as deputy director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 契丹請和，以為賀正旦使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sought peace, he was appointed envoy to congratulate them on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sued for peace, he was sent as envoy to offer New Year's congratulations.

sentences.zh: 真宗方幸西京，維還詣行在，具言其待遇禮厚，必保盟好。

translations.literal: Zhenzong was then visiting the Western Capital; Wei returned to the traveling palace and fully reported that they had been treated with great courtesy and would surely preserve the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong was then at the Western Capital. Wei came back to the imperial camp and reported in detail that the Khitan had received him with great courtesy and would surely keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy director of the Ministry of War and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy director of the Ministry of War and appointed drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 自是每北使至，多命維主之。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever northern envoys arrived, Wei was often ordered to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever envoys came from the north, Wei was usually the one chosen to receive them.

sentences.zh: 擢為翰林學士，累遷中書舍人，以疾辭，出知許州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician, successively rose to Secretariat drafter, then citing illness resigned and went out as prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin Academician and eventually to Secretariat drafter, but then pleaded illness, left court, and became prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復入翰林為學士承旨，加史館修撰。

translations.literal: He reentered the Hanlin Academy as chief academician and was additionally made compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Hanlin Academy as chief academician and was also named a compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，再遷為尚書左丞兼侍讀學士，預修《真宗實錄》，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renzong's reign he was again promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and reader-in-waiting, participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Zhenzong, and was transferred to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Renzong's reign he was promoted again to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and reader-in-waiting, helped compile the Veritable Records of Zhenzong, and was then made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 會塞下傳契丹將絕盟，復遣維往使。

translations.literal: When reports came from the frontier that the Khitan would break the alliance, Wei was again sent as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier reports said the Khitan meant to renounce the treaty, Wei was dispatched north once more.

sentences.zh: 其主隆緒重維名，館勞加禮，使賦《兩朝悠久詩》。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler Longxu, respecting Wei's reputation, entertained him with extra courtesy and had him compose the Poem on the Enduring Friendship of Two Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler Longxu, who held Wei in high regard, received him with exceptional honors and asked him to compose the Poem on the Enduring Friendship of Two Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 詩成，大喜。

translations.literal: When the poem was completed, Longxu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the poem was finished, Longxu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 既還，帝欲用為樞密副使，或斥維賦詩自稱小臣，乃寢。

translations.literal: After he returned, the emperor wished to appoint him deputy commissioner of military affairs, but someone criticized him for calling himself "this petty subject" in the poem, and the appointment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: After his return the emperor wanted to make him deputy commissioner of military affairs, but critics seized on his use of the phrase "this petty subject" in the poem, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，辭不拜，引李士衡故事求換官，除相州觀察使，為諫官劉隨所詆，知亳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of justice, declined to accept, cited Li Shihang's precedent in requesting a different post, was appointed military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, was slandered by remonstrance official Liu Sui, and was made prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of justice but refused the appointment, citing Li Shihang's precedent in asking for a different post. He was made military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, then attacked by remonstrance official Liu Sui and reassigned as prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請赴本鎮，改河陽。

translations.literal: He requested to take up his assigned command and was transferred to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go to his post in person and was reassigned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 久之還朝，復出知陳州，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he returned to court, then went out again as prefect of Chen Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he returned to court, then went out once more as prefect of Chen Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 維博學，少以文章知名，至老手不廢書。

translations.literal: Wei was broadly learned; from youth he was known for his literary work, and even in old age he never put books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was deeply learned. He had been known for his writing since youth, and even in old age he never stopped reading.

sentences.zh: 景德以後，巡幸四方，典章名物，多維所參定。

translations.literal: After the Jingde era, when the emperor toured in all directions, Wei participated in determining many ritual codes and named objects.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jingde period, when the court traveled widely, Wei helped settle many questions of ritual and nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 嘗預定《七經正義》，修《續通典》、《冊府元龜》。

translations.literal: He had participated in establishing the Correct Meanings of the Seven Classics and in compiling the Continued Comprehensive Institutions and the Precious Tortoise of the Imperial Archives.
translations.idiomatic: He had helped establish the Correct Meanings of the Seven Classics and had worked on the Continued Comprehensive Institutions and the Precious Tortoise of the Imperial Archives.

sentences.zh: 性寬易，喜慍不見於色，獎借後進，嗜酒善謔，而好為詩。

translations.literal: By nature he was easygoing; joy and anger did not show on his face; he encouraged younger scholars; he loved wine and witty banter, and enjoyed composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was easygoing by nature, never showing pleasure or anger on his face, and he generously encouraged younger men. He loved wine and good humor, and he delighted in writing poetry.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「人生觴詠自適，餘何營哉？」

translations.literal: He often said: "In life, to drink and recite poetry for one's own contentment—what else is there to pursue?"
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "In this life, all I need is wine and verse for my own pleasure. What else is worth striving for?"

sentences.zh: 既沒，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: After he died, the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his household had nothing left over.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou he was posthumously awarded right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyou he was posthumously given the title of right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子師錫，虞部員外郎；

translations.literal: His son Shixi served as deputy director of the Directorate of Parks and Buildings;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixi was deputy director of the Directorate of Parks and Buildings;

sentences.zh: 公謹，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Gongjin served as attendant in the Heir Apparent's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin was an attendant in the Heir Apparent's Palace.

sentences.zh: 王旦，字子明，大名莘人。

translations.literal: Wang Dan, styled Ziming, was a native of Shen County in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan, styled Ziming, came from Shen County in Daming.

sentences.zh: 曾祖言，黎陽令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan was magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan had been magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 祖徹，左拾遺。

translations.literal: His grandfather Che was left reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Che had served as left reminder at court.

sentences.zh: 父祐，尚書兵部侍郎，以文章顯於漢、周之際，事太祖、太宗為名臣。

translations.literal: His father You was vice minister of war in the Department of State Affairs; renowned for literary talent during the transition between Later Han and Zhou; he served Taizu and Taizong as a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was vice minister of war. Famous for his writing in the years between Later Han and Zhou, he served Taizu and Taizong and was counted among the great ministers of the age.

sentences.zh: 嘗諭杜重威使無反漢，拒盧多遜害趙普之謀，以百口明符彥卿無罪，世多稱其陰德。

translations.literal: He once admonished Du Chongwei not to rebel against Later Han, refused Lu Duoxun's plot against Zhao Pu, and vouched with his family's lives that Fu Yanqing was innocent; the world often praised his hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He once warned Du Chongwei against rebelling against Later Han, blocked Lu Duoxun's plot to destroy Zhao Pu, and staked his family's lives on Fu Yanqing's innocence. People widely praised his quiet moral force.

sentences.zh: 祐手植三槐於庭，曰：「吾之後世，必有為三公者，此其所以志也。」

translations.literal: You personally planted three pagoda trees in the courtyard and said: "In later generations of my line there will surely be one who reaches the Three Dukes—this is what I plant to remember."
translations.idiomatic: Wang You planted three pagoda trees in the courtyard with his own hands and said, "A descendant of mine will one day reach the rank of the Three Dukes. These trees are my memorial to that hope."

sentences.zh: 旦幼沉默，好學有文，祐器之曰：「此兒當至公相。」

translations.literal: Dan from youth was quiet and reserved, fond of learning and accomplished in letters; You treasured him and said: "This boy will reach minister and chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Dan was quiet and studious from boyhood and showed early literary talent. You prized him and said, "This child will rise to minister and chancellor."

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，進士及第，為大理評事、知平江縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Pingjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and was made a case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Pingjiang County.

sentences.zh: 其廨舊傳有物怪憑戾，居多不寧。

translations.literal: The office was traditionally said to be haunted by strange creatures causing disturbances; those who lived there were mostly unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate's quarters were long rumored to be haunted, and few who occupied them found any peace.

sentences.zh: 旦將至前夕，守吏聞群鬼嘯呼云：「相君至矣，當避去。」

translations.literal: On the eve of Dan's arrival, the caretaker heard ghosts howling: "The minister is coming—we must depart."
translations.idiomatic: On the night before Dan arrived, the caretaker heard spirits wailing, "The minister is coming. We must leave."

sentences.zh: 自是遂絕。

translations.literal: From then on the disturbances ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that the hauntings stopped.

sentences.zh: 就改將作監丞。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he was reassigned as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言為轉運使，以威望自任，屬吏屏畏，入旦境，稱其善政，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Zhao Changyan served as transport commissioner and relied on his prestige; subordinates feared him; entering Dan's jurisdiction, he praised his good governance and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changyan, then transport commissioner, carried himself with intimidating authority and kept his subordinates in awe. When he entered Dan's district he praised his governance and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 代還，命監潭州銀場。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was ordered to supervise the silver yard at Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour of duty ended and he returned to the capital, he was assigned to supervise the silver yard at Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 何承矩典郡，薦入為著作佐郎，預編《文苑英華》、《詩類》。

translations.literal: He Chenuju governed the prefecture and recommended him for entry as assistant compiler; he participated in compiling Splendors of the Literary Garden and Categories of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He Chenuju, then prefect, recommended him for appointment as assistant compiler, and he took part in compiling Splendors of the Literary Garden and Categories of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中丞、通判鄭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace secretariat director and vice prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace secretariat director and made vice prefect of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 表請天下建常平倉，以塞兼並之路。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Ever-Normal Granaries be established throughout the empire to block the path of land consolidation.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking that Ever-Normal Granaries be established across the empire to check the spread of land consolidation.

sentences.zh: 徙濠州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，王禹偁薦其才任轉運使，驛召至京，旦不樂吏職，獻文。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, Wang Yucheng recommended his talent for transport commissioner; he was summoned urgently to the capital; Dan did not enjoy administrative office and submitted literary work.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era Wang Yucheng recommended him for transport commissioner. Summoned posthaste to the capital, Dan, who had little taste for administrative duty, submitted literary work instead.

sentences.zh: 召試，命直史館。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination and appointed to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After an imperial examination he was appointed to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜右正言、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed right remonstrance official and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became right remonstrance official and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 初，祐以宿名久掌書命，旦不十年繼其任，時論美之。

translations.literal: Earlier, You by virtue of established reputation had long managed imperial writing; Dan within less than ten years succeeded to his post; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: You, already famous, had long held the post of imperial scribe; Dan succeeded him in less than ten years, and contemporaries admired the succession.

sentences.zh: 錢若水有人倫鑒，見旦曰：「真宰相器也。」

translations.literal: Qian Ruoshui had discerning judgment of character; seeing Dan he said: "Truly the makings of a chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ruoshui was a keen judge of men. When he saw Dan he said, "Here is true chancellor timber."

sentences.zh: 與之同列，每曰：「王君淩霄聳壑，棟梁之材，貴不可涯，非吾所及。」

translations.literal: Serving together in the same office, he would often say: "Master Wang towers like clouds over ravines—timber for roof-beams; his eminence is boundless—not something I can match."
translations.idiomatic: Serving beside him, Qian would often say, "Master Wang rises like cloud-capped peaks—beam timber for the state. His stature has no limit. I cannot compare."

sentences.zh: 李沆以同年生，亦推重為遠大之器。

translations.literal: Li Hang, as a fellow examination graduate, also esteemed him as a man of far-reaching capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang, who had passed the examinations in the same year, likewise regarded him as a man of great future promise.

sentences.zh: 明年，與蘇易簡同知貢舉，加虞部員外郎、同判吏部流內銓、知考課院。

translations.literal: The following year, together with Su Yijian he supervised the civil examinations; he was additionally appointed deputy director of the Directorate of Parks and Buildings, co-administrator of personnel lists in the Ministry of Personnel, and director of the Performance Evaluation Office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he and Su Yijian jointly supervised the civil examinations. He was also made deputy director of the Directorate of Parks and Buildings, co-administrator of the Ministry of Personnel's roster office, and director of the performance evaluation bureau.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言參機務，旦避嫌，引唐獨孤鬱、權德輿故事辭職。

translations.literal: When Zhao Changyan entered confidential state affairs, Dan avoided suspicion by citing the Tang precedents of Dugu Yu and Quan Deyu in resigning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Changyan entered the inner councils of state, Dan stepped aside to avoid suspicion, citing the Tang examples of Dugu Yu and Quan Deyu.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其識體，改禮部郎中、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his sense of propriety and changed his appointment to director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong admired his propriety and reassigned him as director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 昌言出知鳳翔，即日以旦知制誥，仍兼修撰、判院事，面賜金紫，擇牯犀帶寵之，又令冠西閣。

translations.literal: When Changyan went out as prefect of Fengxiang, that same day Dan was made drafter of edicts, still concurrently compiler and administrator of the institute; he was personally granted gold and purple, given a chosen rhinoceros-horn belt to honor him, and also ordered to head the Western Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Changyan left to govern Fengxiang, Dan was that same day made drafter of edicts while retaining his posts as compiler and institute administrator. The emperor personally bestowed gold and purple insignia, chose a rhinoceros-horn belt to honor him, and placed him at the head of the Western Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，知理檢院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he managed the Censorate Investigation Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao he was put in charge of the Censorate Investigation Office.

sentences.zh: 二年，進兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜中書舍人，數月，為翰林學士兼知審官院、通進銀臺封駁司。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Dan was appointed Secretariat drafter; within months he became Hanlin Academician concurrently administering the Appointments Review Office and the Silver Terrace Memorial Transmission and Veto Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne, Dan was appointed Secretariat drafter. Within a few months he was made Hanlin Academician and given charge of the Appointments Review Office and the Silver Terrace Memorial Transmission and Veto Office.

sentences.zh: 帝素賢旦，嘗奏事退，目送之曰：「為朕致太平者，必斯人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor had long regarded Dan as worthy; once after he finished reporting on business and withdrew, the emperor watched him go and said: "The one who will bring peace for me will surely be this man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long admired Dan. Once, after Dan withdrew from an audience, Zhenzong watched him leave and said, "The man who will bring me peace will be this one."

sentences.zh: 錢若水罷樞務，得對苑中，訪近臣之可用者，若水言：「旦有德望，堪任大事。」

translations.literal: When Qian Ruoshui left military affairs and had audience in the garden, he asked which recent ministers were usable; Ruoshui said: "Dan has virtue and prestige—he can undertake great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Ruoshui left the military commission and was received in the imperial garden, the emperor asked which recent ministers were fit for high office. Ruoshui answered, "Dan has both virtue and standing. He can bear great responsibility."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此固朕心所屬也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is indeed where my heart already rests."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is already where my own mind rests."

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，又知貢舉，鎖宿旬日，拜給事中、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he again supervised the examinations, was locked in for ten days, and was appointed censor-in-chief and co-deputy commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he again supervised the examinations, spending ten days sequestered in the examination hall, and was then appointed censor-in-chief and co-deputy commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以工部侍郎參知政事。

translations.literal: The following year, as vice minister of works he became vice grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as vice minister of works, he became vice grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，從幸澶州。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the border, he accompanied the emperor to Chuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the frontier, he accompanied the emperor to Chuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍王元份留守東京，遇暴疾，命旦馳還，權留守事。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Yuanfen held the eastern capital in reserve duty; he suddenly fell gravely ill; Dan was ordered to hurry back and act as reserve custodian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Yuanfen was left to guard the eastern capital when he was suddenly stricken with a grave illness. Dan was ordered to ride back at once and serve as acting custodian of the capital.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「願宣寇準，臣有所陳。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "I wish to summon Kou Zhun—your servant has something to report."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "I ask that Kou Zhun be summoned. Your servant has something to lay before the throne."

sentences.zh: 準至，旦奏曰：「十日之間未有捷報，時當如何？」

translations.literal: When Zhun arrived, Dan memorialized: "If within ten days there is no favorable report, what should be done at that time?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhun arrived, Dan said, "If no good news comes within ten days, what then should be done?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然良久，曰：「立皇太子。」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent for a long time, then said: "Install the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent a long while, then said, "Install the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 旦既至京，直入禁中，下令甚嚴，使人不得傳播。

translations.literal: When Dan reached the capital, he went straight into the inner palace; his orders were very strict; people were not allowed to spread rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dan reached the capital he went directly into the inner palace and issued stern orders forbidding anyone to spread rumors.

sentences.zh: 及駕還，旦子弟及家人皆迎於郊，忽聞後有騶訶聲，驚視之，乃旦也。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Dan's children and family all went to the outskirts to welcome him; suddenly they heard shouting from an escort behind; startled, they looked—it was Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, Dan's children and household went out to meet him. Suddenly they heard an escort shouting from behind. Startled, they turned—and it was Dan himself.

sentences.zh: 二年，加尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜工部尚書、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士、監修《兩朝國史》。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed minister of works, same aspects of the Three Departments coordinator, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and supervisor of compilation of the National History of Two Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made minister of works, coordinator of the Three Departments, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and supervisor of the National History of Two Reigns.

sentences.zh: 契丹既受盟，寇準以為功，有自得之色，真宗亦自得也。

translations.literal: After the Khitan accepted the alliance, Kou Zhun took it as his achievement and wore a self-satisfied look; Zhenzong too was self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Khitan had accepted the treaty, Kou Zhun treated it as his own triumph and looked thoroughly pleased with himself—and Zhenzong was pleased as well.

sentences.zh: 王欽若惎準，欲傾之，從容言曰：「此《春秋》城下之盟也，諸侯猶恥之，而陛下以為功，臣竊不取。」

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo harbored jealousy toward Zhun and wished to topple him; he said casually: "This is like the alliance under the city walls in the Spring and Autumn Annals—even feudal lords were ashamed of it, yet Your Majesty takes it as merit; your servant privately cannot approve."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo resented Zhun and sought to bring him down. Speaking with apparent ease, he said, "This is the sort of treaty made beneath the walls of an enemy city that the Spring and Autumn Annals treats as a disgrace. Yet Your Majesty calls it a triumph. I for one cannot accept that."

sentences.zh: 帝愀然曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor looked troubled and said: "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "Then what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 欽若度帝厭兵，即謬曰：「陛下以兵取幽燕，乃可滌恥。」

translations.literal: Qinruo, gauging that the emperor was weary of war, immediately said falsely: "If Your Majesty takes Youyan by force, then shame can be washed away."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's weariness of war, Qinruo at once said, "If Your Majesty retook Youyan by force, the shame would be wiped clean."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「河朔生靈始免兵革，朕安能為此？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The people north of the Yellow River have just been spared from war—how could I do such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The people of Hebei have only just been spared the horrors of war. How could I do that?

sentences.zh: 可思其次。」

translations.literal: Think of another way."
translations.idiomatic: Think of something else."

sentences.zh: 欽若曰：「唯有封禪泰山，可以鎮服四海，誇示外國。

translations.literal: Qinruo said: "Only by performing the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai can one subdue the four seas and display glory to foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo said, "There is only one other course: to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai. That would awe the empire and impress foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 然自古封禪，當得天瑞希世絕倫之事，然後可爾。」

translations.literal: Yet since ancient times, the feng and shan rites required obtaining heaven-sent auspices of unmatched rarity—only then could one proceed."
translations.idiomatic: But since antiquity those rites had required a heavenly portent of unmatched rarity—only then could they be undertaken."

sentences.zh: 既而又曰：「天瑞安可必得？

translations.literal: Then he added: "How can heavenly auspices be surely obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, "Who can guarantee a sign from heaven?

sentences.zh: 前代蓋有以人力為之者，惟人主深信而崇之，以明示天下，則與天瑞無異也。」

translations.literal: In earlier ages there were those who made them by human effort; if the ruler deeply believed and honored them, showing them openly to the world, then they were no different from heavenly auspices."
translations.idiomatic: Past ages had seen such signs manufactured by human contrivance. If the ruler truly believed in them and displayed them to the world, they would serve as well as any heaven-sent omen."

sentences.zh: 帝思久之，乃可，而心憚旦，曰：「王旦得無不可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor pondered long, then assented; but he feared Dan in his heart and said: "Would Wang Dan perhaps not agree?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought for a long time and finally agreed—but he still feared Dan and said, "Surely Wang Dan will refuse?"

sentences.zh: 欽若曰：「臣得以聖意喻之，宜無不可。」

translations.literal: Qinruo said: "Your servant can explain the sage emperor's intent to him—he surely will not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo said, "Leave it to me. If I explain Your Majesty's purpose, he will not stand in the way."

sentences.zh: 乘間為旦言，旦黽勉而從。

translations.literal: Seizing an opportunity he spoke to Dan; Dan reluctantly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He found an opening to speak with Dan, and Dan yielded with visible reluctance.

sentences.zh: 帝猶尤豫，莫與籌之者，會幸秘閣，驟問杜鎬曰：「古所謂河出圖、洛出書，果何事耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor still hesitated, with no one to discuss plans with; chancing to visit the Secret Archive, he suddenly asked Du Hao: "What in ancient times were the 'River yielding the Diagram' and 'Luo yielding the Book'—what were they really?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained undecided and had no one with whom to discuss the matter. On a visit to the Secret Archive he suddenly asked Du Hao, "In antiquity people spoke of the River yielding the Diagram and the Luo yielding the Book. What were those things, really?"

sentences.zh: 鎬老儒，不測其旨，漫應之曰：「此聖人以神道設教爾。」

translations.literal: Du Hao, an old Confucian, did not grasp his intent and answered casually: "This was the sage using the divine way to establish teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Du Hao, an elderly scholar, did not catch his drift and answered vaguely, "Those were cases in which the sage taught the people through the language of the divine."

sentences.zh: 帝繇此意決，遂召旦飲，歡甚，賜以尊酒，曰：「此酒極佳，歸與妻孥共之。」

translations.literal: From this the emperor's mind was settled; he then summoned Dan to drink; very joyful; granted fine wine and said: "This wine is excellent—go home and share it with wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: That answer settled the emperor's mind. He summoned Dan to drink with him and, in high spirits, presented him with a jar of fine wine, saying, "This is excellent wine. Take it home and share it with your wife and children."

sentences.zh: 既歸發之，皆珠也。

translations.literal: When he returned and opened it, all were pearls.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan opened the jar at home, he found it filled with pearls.

sentences.zh: 由是凡天書、封禪等事，旦不復異議。

translations.literal: From then on, on all matters of Heavenly Writings, feng and shan, and the like, Dan no longer raised objections.
translations.idiomatic: After that Dan never again objected to the Heavenly Writings, the feng and shan rites, or anything of that kind.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，為天書儀仗使，從封泰山，為大禮使，進中書侍郎兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he served as commissioner of Heavenly Writings protocol; accompanied the feng rite at Mount Tai; served as grand rites commissioner; and advanced to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was made commissioner of Heavenly Writings protocol, accompanied the feng rite at Mount Tai as grand rites commissioner, and was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 受詔撰《封祀壇頌》，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He received command to compose the Eulogy of the Sacrificial Altar for the Feng Rite and was additionally appointed minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he wrote the Eulogy of the Sacrificial Altar for the Feng Rite and was further made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 四年，祀汾陰，又為大禮使，遷右僕射、昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when sacrificing at Fenyin, he again served as grand rites commissioner and was transferred to right vice director and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the sacrifice was performed at Fenyin, he again served as grand rites commissioner and was promoted to right vice director and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 仍撰《祠壇頌》，將復進秩，懇辭得免，止加功臣。

translations.literal: He also composed the Eulogy of the Sacrificial Altar; about to be promoted again in rank, he earnestly declined and was excused; only the title of meritorious subject was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Eulogy of the Sacrificial Altar. When another promotion was proposed, he begged off and was allowed to decline; he received only the title of meritorious subject.

sentences.zh: 俄兼門下侍郎、玉清昭應宮使。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he concurrently served as vice director of the Chancellery and commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made vice director of the Chancellery and commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年，為玉清奉聖像大禮使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as grand rites commissioner for presenting the sacred image at Yujing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was grand rites commissioner for the presentation of the sacred image at Yujing.

sentences.zh: 景靈宮建，又為朝修使。

translations.literal: When the Jingling Palace was built, he again served as commissioner for court rituals of construction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingling Palace was erected, he again served as commissioner overseeing its court rituals.

sentences.zh: 七年，刻天書，兼刻玉使，選御廄三馬賜之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he engraved the Heavenly Book, concurrently served as Jade-Carving Envoy, and three horses from the imperial stables were selected and granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he oversaw the engraving of the Heavenly Book, served concurrently as Jade-Carving Envoy, and was granted three horses from the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮成，拜司空。

translations.literal: When the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace was completed, he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace was completed, he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 京師賜酺，旦以慘恤不赴會，帝賜詩導意焉。

translations.literal: The capital was granted a celebratory feast; Dan, out of grief and mourning, did not attend; the emperor bestowed a poem to guide his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was granted a court feast, Dan declined to attend out of grief, and the emperor sent him a poem to console him.

sentences.zh: 《國史》成，遷司空。

translations.literal: When the National History was completed, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the National History was completed, he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 旦為天書使，每有大禮，輒奉天書以行，恒邑邑不樂。

translations.literal: As Heavenly Book envoy, whenever there was a great ritual, he would carry the Heavenly Book on the journey, always anxious and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: As Heavenly Book envoy, whenever a great ceremony required it he bore the Heavenly Book on the procession—and was always inwardly troubled and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 凡柄用十八年，為相僅一紀。

translations.literal: In all he wielded power for eighteen years, serving as chancellor for only one twelve-year cycle.
translations.idiomatic: In all he held power for eighteen years, yet served as chief minister for only twelve.

sentences.zh: 會契丹修和，西夏誓守故地，二邊兵罷不用，真宗以無事治天下。

translations.literal: When the Khitan renewed peace and Western Xia swore to hold their former territory, troops on both frontiers were disbanded and unused; Zhenzong governed the realm as though nothing troubled it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Khitan renewed the peace and Western Xia pledged to keep to their old borders, armies on both frontiers were stood down, and Zhenzong ruled the realm as though at peace.

sentences.zh: 旦謂祖宗之法具在，務行故事，慎所變改。

translations.literal: Dan held that the laws of the founding emperors were all still in place; one should follow established precedent and be cautious about what one changed.
translations.idiomatic: Dan held that the founding emperors' institutions remained intact: one should follow precedent and change things only with great caution.

sentences.zh: 帝久益信之，言無不聽，凡大臣有所請，必曰：「王旦以為如何？」

translations.literal: Over time the emperor trusted him all the more and never rejected his words; whenever a minister made a request, he would always say: "What does Wang Dan think?"
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor came to trust him completely and never refused his counsel; whenever a minister petitioned for something, he would always ask, "What does Wang Dan think?"

sentences.zh: 旦與人寡言笑，默坐終日，及奏事，群臣異同，旦徐一言以定。

translations.literal: Dan spoke little and laughed rarely with others, sitting in silence all day; yet when presenting business, if the ministers disagreed, a single slow remark from Dan would settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan spoke little and seldom laughed; he would sit in silence all day. Yet when business came before the throne and the ministers were divided, one quiet word from him would settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 歸家，或不去冠帶，入靜室獨坐，家人莫敢見之。

translations.literal: Returning home, he sometimes did not remove cap and belt, entered a quiet room and sat alone, and no member of his household dared to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At home he sometimes kept on his official cap and belt, withdrew to a private room, and sat alone—no one in his household dared disturb him.

sentences.zh: 旦弟以問趙安仁，安仁曰：「方議事，公不欲行而未決，此必憂朝廷矣。」

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother asked Zhao Anren about it; Anren said: "He is just deliberating on state affairs. The lord does not wish to proceed but has not yet decided—he must be troubled over the court."
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger brother asked Zhao Anren what this meant. Anren said, "He is weighing a matter of state. Your brother does not want to act but has not yet decided against it—he must be brooding over the court."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗示二府《喜雨詩》，旦袖歸曰：「上詩有一字誤寫，莫進入改卻否？」

translations.literal: The emperor once showed the Two Departments his "Joy for Rain" poem; Dan put it in his sleeve and took it home, saying: "There is one miswritten character in His Majesty's poem—shall I send it in to have it corrected?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once showed his "Joy for Rain" poem to the Two Departments. Dan tucked it into his sleeve and said on his way home, "There is one miswritten character in the poem—shall I submit it for correction?"

sentences.zh: 王欽若曰：「此亦無害。」

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo said: "This is also harmless."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said, "That hardly matters."

sentences.zh: 而密奏之，帝慍，謂旦曰：「昨日詩有誤字，何不來奏？」

translations.literal: Yet he secretly memorialized about it; the emperor was displeased and said to Dan: "Yesterday's poem had a wrong character—why did you not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qinruo secretly memorialized about it. The emperor was displeased and said to Dan, "Yesterday's poem had a wrong character—why did you not tell me?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「臣得詩未暇再閱，有失上陳。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "When I received the poem I had no leisure to read it again; there was a lapse in reporting it to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "When I received the poem I had no time to read it again, and I failed to report it to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 惶懼再拜謝，諸臣皆拜，獨樞密馬知節不拜，具以實奏，且曰：「王旦略不辨，真宰相器也。」

translations.literal: In fear he bowed twice in thanks; all the ministers bowed, but only Privy Councillor Ma Zhijie did not bow, reporting the full truth and saying: "Wang Dan scarcely distinguished it at all—he truly has the bearing of a chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Dan bowed twice in fear and apology; the other ministers bowed as well, but Privy Councillor Ma Zhijie alone did not. He reported what had actually happened and said, "Wang Dan could barely tell the difference—that is the mark of a true chancellor."

sentences.zh: 帝顧旦而笑焉。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to look at Dan and smiled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Dan and smiled.

sentences.zh: 天下大蝗，使人於野得死蝗，帝以示大臣。

translations.literal: Locusts ravaged the realm; an envoy found dead locusts in the fields, and the emperor showed them to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts plagued the empire. An envoy found dead locusts in the countryside, and the emperor showed them to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 明日，執政遂袖死蝗進曰：「蝗實死矣，請示於朝，率百官賀。」

translations.literal: The next day the chief ministers carried dead locusts in their sleeves and presented them, saying: "The locusts are indeed dead—please display this at court and lead all officials in congratulation."
