translations.idiomatic: The next day the chief ministers brought dead locusts tucked in their sleeves and said, "The locusts are truly dead—please show this at court and let all officials offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 旦獨不可。

translations.literal: Dan alone disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Dan alone objected.

sentences.zh: 後數日，方奏事，飛蝗蔽天，帝顧旦曰：「使百官方賀，而蝗如此，豈不為天下笑耶？」

translations.literal: Several days later, while presenting business, flying locusts blotted out the sky; the emperor turned to Dan and said: "If I had let all officials offer congratulations while the locusts were like this, would I not have been laughed at by the whole realm?"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, while they were presenting business, locusts blotted out the sky. The emperor turned to Dan and said, "If I had let the whole court congratulate me while the locusts were still like this, would not the realm have laughed at me?"

sentences.zh: 宮禁火災，旦馳入，帝曰：「兩朝所積，朕不妄費，一朝殆盡，誠可惜也。」

translations.literal: A fire broke out in the palace precincts; Dan hurried in. The emperor said: "What two reigns had accumulated—I never wasted it—in one morning it was nearly all gone; truly this is lamentable."
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the palace precincts, Dan rushed in. The emperor said, "Two reigns' worth of accumulation—and I never squandered it—in one morning it was nearly gone. This is truly a pity."

sentences.zh: 旦對曰：「陛下富有天下，財帛不足憂，所慮者政令賞罰之不當。

translations.literal: Dan replied: "Your Majesty possesses the whole realm; wealth is no cause for worry. What should concern you is whether edicts, rewards, and punishments are not right.
translations.idiomatic: Dan replied, "Your Majesty possesses the whole realm; wealth is no cause for worry. What should concern you is whether your edicts, rewards, and punishments are just.

sentences.zh: 臣備位宰府，天災如此，臣當罷免。」

translations.literal: I hold office in the chancellery to no effect; with a heavenly disaster such as this, I ought to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: I hold a chancellor's post to no good effect; with a disaster of heaven such as this, I ought to be removed."

sentences.zh: 繼上表待罪，帝乃降詔罪己，許中外封事言得失。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial accepting blame; the emperor thereupon issued an edict blaming himself and permitted memorials from within and without on merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial accepting blame. The emperor issued an edict blaming himself and allowed officials throughout the realm to submit memorials on what was right and wrong in government.

sentences.zh: 後有言榮王宮火所延，非天災，請置獄劾，當坐死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Later someone said the fire had spread from the Prince of Rong's palace and was not a heavenly disaster; they requested an investigation and prosecution, with more than a hundred liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone claimed the fire had spread from the Prince of Rong's palace and was not a heaven-sent calamity, and asked that an inquiry be opened—more than a hundred people faced execution.

sentences.zh: 旦獨請曰：「始火時，陛下已罪己詔天下，臣等皆上章待罪。

translations.literal: Dan alone petitioned, saying: "When the fire first broke out, Your Majesty had already issued an edict blaming yourself to the realm, and we all submitted memorials accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: Dan alone petitioned, saying, "When the fire first broke out, Your Majesty had already issued an edict blaming yourself to the realm, and we all submitted memorials accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 今反歸咎於人，何以示信？

translations.literal: Now to turn and blame others—how is trust to be shown?
translations.idiomatic: Now to turn and blame others—how can Your Majesty show good faith?

sentences.zh: 且火雖有跡，寧知非天譴耶？」

translations.literal: Moreover, though the fire left traces, who is to say it was not heavenly castigation?"
translations.idiomatic: And though the fire left traces, who can say it was not heaven's rebuke?"

sentences.zh: 當坐者皆免。

translations.literal: All who would have been punished were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: All who would have been punished were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 日者上書言宮禁事，坐誅，籍其家，得朝士所與往還占問吉凶之說。

translations.literal: A diviner memorialized about palace affairs, was executed for it, and when his household was confiscated there were found among his papers fortune-telling exchanges with court officials on auspice and ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: A diviner memorialized about palace affairs and was executed. When his property was confiscated, officials found among his papers exchanges with court gentlemen seeking divinations on fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲付御史問狀，旦曰：「此人之常情，且語不及朝廷，不足罪。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to hand the case to the censorate for investigation; Dan said: "This is ordinary human feeling, and their talk did not touch on the court—it does not warrant punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and wanted the censorate to investigate. Dan said, "This is ordinary human nature, and their talk never touched on court affairs—it does not warrant punishment."

sentences.zh: 真宗怒不解，旦因自取嘗所占問之書進曰：「臣少賤時，不免為此。

translations.literal: Zhenzong's anger did not abate; Dan thereupon took his own former fortune-telling papers and presented them, saying: "When I was young and lowly, I could not avoid doing this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong's anger did not lift. Dan then produced his own old fortune-telling papers and said, "When I was young and obscure, I could not avoid doing this myself.

sentences.zh: 必以為罪，願並臣付獄。」

translations.literal: If it must be treated as a crime, I ask that I too be handed over to prison."
translations.idiomatic: If this must be treated as a crime, then send me to prison as well."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「此事已發，何可免？」

translations.literal: Zhenzong said: "This matter has already come to light—how can it be excused?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "This matter has already come to light—how can it be excused?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「臣為宰相執國法，豈可自為之，幸於不發而以罪人。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "I serve as chancellor and enforce the laws of the state—how could I do this myself yet, relying on its not coming to light, treat others as criminals."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "I serve as chancellor and enforce the laws of the state—how could I do this myself and then, because mine never came to light, treat others as criminals?"

sentences.zh: 帝意解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 旦至中書，悉焚所得書。

translations.literal: When Dan reached the Central Secretariat, he burned all the confiscated papers.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan reached the Central Secretariat, he burned all the confiscated papers.

sentences.zh: 既而復悔，馳取之，而已焚之矣，由是皆免。

translations.literal: Presently he regretted it and galloped to retrieve them—but they had already been burned, and by this all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and galloped back to recover them, but they were already ashes—and so everyone was spared.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，太子諭德見旦，稱太子學書有法。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, the Tutor to the Crown Prince saw Dan and praised the prince's calligraphy as methodical.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, his tutor visited Dan and praised the prince's calligraphy as well disciplined.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「諭德之職，止於是耶？」

translations.literal: Dan said: "Is the tutorship's duty only this much?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Is the tutor's duty only to say this much?"

sentences.zh: 張士遜又稱太子書，旦曰：「太子不在應舉，選學士不在學書。」

translations.literal: Zhang Shisun again praised the prince's calligraphy; Dan said: "The crown prince is not sitting for the examinations—choosing scholars is not about studying penmanship."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shisun again praised the prince's calligraphy. Dan said, "The crown prince is not sitting for the civil examinations—a chosen scholar is not chosen for his penmanship."

sentences.zh: 契丹奏請歲給外別假錢幣。

translations.literal: The Khitan memorialized requesting an additional loan of coin and silk beyond the annual tribute stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan memorialized asking for an extra loan of silk and coin beyond the annual tribute quota.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「東封甚近，車駕將出，彼以此探朝廷之意耳。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "The eastern tour is very near and the imperial carriage is about to depart—they are using this to probe the court's intentions."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "The eastern tour is close at hand and the imperial carriage is about to set out—they are using this to sound out the court's intentions."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何以答之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How should we answer?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How should we answer?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「止當以微物而輕之。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "We should respond only with something trivial and treat it lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "We should answer with something trifling and treat the request lightly."

sentences.zh: 乃以歲給三十萬物內各借三萬，仍諭次年額內除之。

translations.literal: Accordingly, from within the annual allotment of three hundred thousand items, three ten thousand of each were lent, and they were told the amount would be deducted from next year's quota.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, from within the annual tribute of three hundred thousand units, three ten thousand of each category were lent, with notice that the sum would be deducted from the following year's quota.

sentences.zh: 契丹得之，大慚。

translations.literal: When the Khitan received this, they were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan received this reply, they were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 次年，復下有司：「契丹所借金幣六萬，事屬微末，今仍依常數與之，後不為比。」

translations.literal: The next year, orders were again sent to the relevant offices: "The sixty thousand in gold and silk borrowed by the Khitan is a trivial matter; grant it now according to the regular quota, but let this not serve as precedent hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: The next year the throne again instructed the relevant offices: "The Khitan's borrowed sixty thousand in gold and silk is a trifling matter; grant it according to the usual quota, but let this not become a precedent."

sentences.zh: 西夏趙德明言民饑，求糧百萬斛，大臣皆曰：「德明新納誓而敢違，請以詔責之。」

translations.literal: Western Xia's Zhao Deming reported that the people were starving and requested a million hu of grain; the ministers all said: "Deming has newly sworn allegiance yet dares to defy us—please rebuke him by edict."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deming of Western Xia reported that his people were starving and asked for a million hu of grain. The ministers all said, "Deming has only just sworn allegiance and already dares to press us—rebuke him by edict."

sentences.zh: 帝以問旦，旦請敕有司具粟百萬於京師，而詔德明來取之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Dan; Dan requested that the relevant offices prepare a million hu of grain at the capital and that Deming be instructed by edict to come and take it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Dan. Dan requested that the relevant offices stock a million hu of grain at the capital and that Deming be instructed by edict to come and fetch it.

sentences.zh: 德明得詔，慚且拜曰：「朝廷有人。」

translations.literal: When Deming received the edict, ashamed he bowed and said: "The court has capable men."
translations.idiomatic: When Deming received the edict, he bowed in shame and said, "The court has men of ability."

sentences.zh: 寇準數短旦，旦專稱準。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun repeatedly spoke ill of Dan, yet Dan exclusively praised Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun repeatedly disparaged Dan, yet Dan never failed to speak well of Zhun.

sentences.zh: 帝謂旦曰：「卿雖稱其美，彼專談卿惡。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Dan: "Though you praise his merits, he speaks only of your faults."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Dan, "You praise his virtues, but he speaks only of your faults."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「理固當然。

translations.literal: Dan said: "It is only as reason demands.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "That is only as it should be.

sentences.zh: 臣在相位久，政事闕失必多。

translations.literal: I have long been in the chancellorship, and my failures in governance must be many.
translations.idiomatic: I have long served as chancellor, and my failures in government must be many.

sentences.zh: 準對陛下無所隱，益見其忠直，此臣所以重準也。」

translations.literal: Zhun hides nothing from Your Majesty, which all the more shows his loyalty and forthrightness—this is why I esteem Zhun."
translations.idiomatic: Zhun hides nothing before Your Majesty, which all the more shows his loyalty and directness—that is why I value him."

sentences.zh: 帝以是愈賢旦。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby esteemed Dan all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereby thought even more highly of Dan.

sentences.zh: 中書有事送密院，違詔格，準在密院，以事上聞。

translations.literal: When the Central Secretariat sent a matter to the Privy Council in violation of edict regulations, Zhun, who was in the Privy Council, reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Secretariat forwarded a matter to the Privy Council in violation of edict regulations, Zhun, serving in the Privy Council, reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 旦被責，第拜謝，堂吏皆見罰。

translations.literal: Dan was reproved and merely bowed in thanks; all the hall clerks were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was rebuked and simply bowed in acceptance; all the secretariat clerks were punished.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，密院有事送中書，亦違詔格，堂吏欣然呈旦，旦令送還密院。

translations.literal: Within less than a month, when the Privy Council sent a matter to the Central Secretariat that also violated edict regulations, the hall clerks gladly presented it to Dan; Dan ordered it sent back to the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later, when the Privy Council sent a matter to the Central Secretariat that also violated edict regulations, the secretariat clerks eagerly brought it to Dan—but Dan ordered it returned to the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 準大慚，見旦曰：「同年，甚得許大度量？」

translations.literal: Zhun was deeply ashamed; seeing Dan he said: "Fellow graduate—how can you be so magnanimous?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhun was deeply ashamed. Seeing Dan, he said, "Fellow graduate—how can you be so magnanimous?"

sentences.zh: 旦不答。

translations.literal: Dan did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Dan made no reply.

sentences.zh: 寇準罷樞密使，託人私求為使相，旦驚曰：「將相之任，豈可求耶！

translations.literal: When Kou Zhun was dismissed as Privy Councillor, he asked someone privately to seek the post of commissioner with the rank of councilor; Dan was startled and said: "The charge of general and minister—how can it be sought!
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun was removed as Privy Councillor, he had someone privately ask that he be made a military commissioner with concurrent councilor rank. Dan was startled and said, "The posts of general and minister—how can they be sought!

sentences.zh: 吾不受私請。」

translations.literal: I do not accept private requests."
translations.idiomatic: I do not honor private requests."

sentences.zh: 準深憾之。

translations.literal: Zhun resented this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun resented this bitterly.

sentences.zh: 已而除準武勝軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long Zhun was appointed Military Commissioner of Wusheng Circuit and Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhun was appointed military commissioner of Wusheng Circuit and concurrent grand councilor of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 準入見，謝曰：「非陛下知臣，安能至此？」

translations.literal: When Zhun entered audience, he thanked him, saying: "Had Your Majesty not understood me, how could I have reached this point?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhun came before the throne, he thanked the emperor, saying, "Had Your Majesty not understood me, how could I have reached this?"

sentences.zh: 帝具道旦所以薦者，準愧歎，以為不可及。

translations.literal: The emperor fully explained how Dan had recommended him; Zhun sighed in shame and regarded him as beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then explained in full how Dan had recommended him. Zhun sighed in shame and felt he could never measure up.

sentences.zh: 準在藩鎮，生辰，造山棚大宴，又服用僭侈，為人所奏。

translations.literal: While Zhun was in a border command, on his birthday he erected a mountain pavilion and held a great feast, and his dress and accoutrements were extravagantly beyond his rank; someone memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhun held a frontier command, he built a mountain pavilion for a birthday feast and dressed and equipped himself with princely extravagance; someone memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂旦曰：「寇準每事欲效朕，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Dan: "Kou Zhun wants to imitate me in everything—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and said to Dan, "Kou Zhun wants to imitate me in everything—is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 旦徐對曰：「準誠賢能，無如騃何。」

translations.literal: Dan answered slowly: "Zhun is truly talented and capable—what can one do about his foolishness?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan answered slowly, "Zhun is truly able—what can one do about his foolishness?"

sentences.zh: 真宗意遂解，曰：「然，此正是騃爾。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong's mind was eased and he said: "True—it is exactly this foolishness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong's anger eased, and he said, "Yes—that is exactly his foolishness."

sentences.zh: 遂不問。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士陳彭年呈政府科場條目，旦投之地曰：「內翰得官幾日，乃欲隔截天下進士耶？」

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Chen Pengnian presented to the government examination regulations; Dan threw them to the ground and said: "How many days has the Academician held office that he already wishes to blockade the realm's examination candidates?"
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Chen Pengnian submitted examination regulations to the chief ministers. Dan threw them to the floor and said, "How many days have you held office, Academician, that you already want to shut out the empire's examination candidates?"

sentences.zh: 彭年皇恐而退。

translations.literal: Pengnian withdrew in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian withdrew in terror.

sentences.zh: 時向敏中同在中書，出彭年所留文字，旦瞑目取紙封之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiang Minzhong was also in the Central Secretariat; when Pengnian's retained documents were produced, Dan closed his eyes, took paper, and sealed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong was then also in the Central Secretariat. When Pengnian's retained papers were produced, Dan closed his eyes, took a sheet of paper, and sealed them away.

sentences.zh: 敏中請一覽，旦曰：「不過興建符瑞圖進爾。」

translations.literal: Minzhong asked to look; Dan said: "Nothing but proposals to build charts of auspicious omens for presentation."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong asked to see them. Dan said, "Nothing but proposals to build charts of auspicious portents for presentation."

sentences.zh: 後彭年與王曾、張知白參預政事，同謂旦曰：「每奏事，其間有不經上覽者，公批旨奉行，恐人言之以為不可。」

translations.literal: Later Pengnian, together with Wang Zeng and Zhang Zhibai as participating administrators of government, jointly said to Dan: "Whenever we present business, some items do not pass before His Majesty's review; you approve instructions and carry them out—we fear people will say this is improper."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Pengnian served with Wang Zeng and Zhang Zhibai as participating administrators, they said together to Dan, "When we present business, some matters never reach the emperor's eyes, yet you approve instructions and carry them out—we fear people will call that improper."

sentences.zh: 旦遜謝而已。

translations.literal: Dan merely deferred with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dan only thanked them deferentially.

sentences.zh: 一日奏對，旦退，曾等稍留，帝驚曰：「有何事不與王旦來？」

translations.literal: One day after presenting business, Dan withdrew while Zeng and the others lingered; the emperor was startled and said: "What business did you not bring Wang Dan for?"
translations.idiomatic: One day, after presenting business, Dan withdrew while Zeng and the others lingered. The emperor was startled and said, "What matter did you not bring Wang Dan for?"

sentences.zh: 皆以前事對。

translations.literal: They all answered regarding the earlier matter.
translations.idiomatic: They all answered with the earlier complaint.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「旦在朕左右多年，朕察之無毫髮私。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Dan has been at my side for many years, and I have observed in him not a hair's breadth of private interest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Dan has been at my side for many years, and I have never seen the slightest trace of private interest in him.

sentences.zh: 自東封後，朕諭以小事一面奉行，卿等謹奉之。」

translations.literal: Since the eastern tour, I have instructed him to carry out minor matters on his own authority—you should all respect that and follow it."
translations.idiomatic: Since the eastern tour I have told him to carry out minor matters on his own authority—you should all respect that and follow it."

sentences.zh: 曾等退而愧謝，旦曰：「正賴諸公規益。」

translations.literal: Zeng and the others withdrew and apologized in shame; Dan said: "It is precisely because I rely on you gentlemen for corrective counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng and the others withdrew and apologized in shame. Dan said, "It is precisely because I rely on you gentlemen for correction."

sentences.zh: 略不介意。

translations.literal: He was not the least concerned.
translations.idiomatic: He did not mind in the least.

sentences.zh: 帝欲相王欽若，旦曰：「欽若遭逢陛下，恩禮已隆，且乞留之樞密，兩府亦均。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Wang Qinruo chancellor; Dan said: "Qinruo has met with Your Majesty's favor and ceremonial honors are already lofty—please keep him in the Privy Council so the Two Departments remain balanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Wang Qinruo chancellor. Dan said, "Qinruo has already received Your Majesty's extraordinary favor and honors—please keep him in the Privy Council so the Two Departments remain balanced.

sentences.zh: 臣見祖宗朝未嘗有南人當國者，雖古稱立賢無方，然須賢士乃可。

translations.literal: I observe that in the reigns of the founding emperors no southerner ever held national power; though antiquity says worthies may be raised without regard to origin, yet only a truly worthy man could do so.
translations.idiomatic: I see that under the founding emperors no southerner ever held national power. Antiquity says worthies may be raised without regard to origin, but only a truly worthy man could justify that.

sentences.zh: 臣為宰相，不敢沮抑人，此亦公議也。」

translations.literal: As chancellor I dare not suppress anyone—this is also the public consensus."
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor I dare not suppress anyone on my own—but this is also the public consensus."

sentences.zh: 真宗遂止。

translations.literal: Zhenzong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong thereupon dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 旦沒後，欽若始大用，語人曰：「為王公遲我十年作宰相。」

translations.literal: After Dan died, Qinruo was first greatly employed; he told others: "Lord Wang delayed my becoming chancellor by ten years."
translations.idiomatic: After Dan died, Qinruo was at last greatly promoted. He told others, "Lord Wang delayed my becoming chancellor by ten years."

sentences.zh: 欽若與陳堯叟、馬知節同在樞府，因奏事忿爭。

translations.literal: Qinruo, together with Chen Yaosou and Ma Zhijie, were all in the Privy Council and quarreled vehemently while presenting business.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo, Chen Yaosou, and Ma Zhijie all served in the Privy Council and quarreled fiercely while presenting business.

sentences.zh: 真宗召旦至，欽若猶嘩不已，知節流涕曰：「願與欽若同下御史府。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong summoned Dan; Qinruo still clamored without cease; Zhijie wept and said: "I wish to go down to the Censorate together with Qinruo."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong summoned Dan. Qinruo still shouted without stopping. Zhijie wept and said, "I wish to go before the censorate together with Qinruo."

sentences.zh: 旦叱欽若使退。

translations.literal: Dan rebuked Qinruo and had him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Dan rebuked Qinruo and made him withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命付獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered them handed over to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered them sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 旦從容曰：「欽若等恃陛下厚顧，上煩譴訶，當行朝典。

translations.literal: Dan said calmly: "Qinruo and the others, relying on Your Majesty's great favor, have troubled you with rebukes—they should be dealt with according to court precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said calmly, "Qinruo and the others, relying on Your Majesty's great favor, have troubled you with their quarrel—they should be dealt with according to court precedent.

sentences.zh: 願且還內，來日取旨。」

translations.literal: Please return to the inner palace for now and take your instructions tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Please return to the inner palace for now and decide tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 明日，召旦前問之，旦曰：「欽若等當黜，未知坐以何罪？」

translations.literal: The next day, summoning Dan forward, the emperor asked him; Dan said: "Qinruo and the others ought to be dismissed, but it is not yet known on what charge?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned Dan forward and asked him. Dan said, "Qinruo and the others ought to be dismissed, but on what charge?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「坐忿爭無禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The charge is angry dispute without propriety."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The charge is quarreling impertinently."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「陛下奄有天下，使大臣坐忿爭無禮之罪，或聞外國，恐無以威遠。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "Your Majesty possesses all under heaven. To have great ministers convicted of the crime of angry dispute without propriety—if this should be heard in foreign states, I fear you will have no means to inspire awe at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Your Majesty rules all under heaven. To convict great ministers of quarreling impertinently—if word of this reaches foreign states, I fear you will lose the power to awe distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿意如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「願至中書，召欽若等宣示陛下含容之意，且戒約之。

translations.literal: Dan said: "I wish to go to the Secretariat, summon Qinruo and the others, announce Your Majesty's intent of forbearance, and also admonish and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Let me go to the Secretariat, summon Qinruo and the others, convey Your Majesty's intent to be magnanimous, and admonish them as well.

sentences.zh: 俟少間，罷之未晚也。」

translations.literal: To wait a little while and dismiss them would not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: To wait a little longer before dismissing them would not be too late."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非卿之言，朕固難忍。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "But for your words, I could hardly have borne it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But for your counsel, I could scarcely have borne it."

sentences.zh: 後月餘，欽若等皆罷。

translations.literal: More than a month later, Qinruo and the others were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later, Qinruo and the others were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 旦嘗與楊億評品人物，億曰：「丁謂久遠當何如？」

translations.literal: Dan once appraised men's characters with Yang Yi. Yi said: "What will Ding Wei be like in the long run?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan once discussed men's characters with Yang Yi. Yi asked, "What will Ding Wei come to in the long run?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「才則才矣，語道則未。

translations.literal: Dan said: "In talent he is talented, but in speaking of the Way he is not yet there.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "He has talent, yes—but he does not yet understand the Way.

sentences.zh: 他日在上位，使有德者助之，庶得終吉；

translations.literal: If one day he rises to high position and men of virtue assist him, he might end well;
translations.idiomatic: If one day he rises high and men of virtue assist him, he might end well;

sentences.zh: 若獨當權，必為身累爾。」

translations.literal: if he holds power alone, he will surely bring trouble upon himself."
translations.idiomatic: but if he holds power alone, he will surely bring trouble upon himself."

sentences.zh: 後謂果如言。

translations.literal: Later Wei proved exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei proved exactly as Dan had said.

sentences.zh: 旦為兗州景靈宮朝修使，內臣周懷政偕行，或乘間請見，旦必俟從者盡至，冠帶出見於堂皇，白事而退。

translations.literal: When Dan served as commissioner for the court renovation of the Jingling Palace at Yanzhou, the inner attendant Zhou Huaizheng traveled with him. Whenever Huaizheng seized an opportunity to request audience, Dan always waited until all his attendants had arrived, then, dressed in cap and sash, came out to receive him in the main hall, reported his business, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan served as commissioner for the court renovation of the Jingling Palace at Yanzhou, the eunuch Zhou Huaizheng traveled with him. Whenever Huaizheng found a moment to request an audience, Dan always waited until every attendant had arrived, then appeared in cap and sash in the main hall, heard his business, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後懷政以事敗，方知旦遠慮。

translations.literal: Later, when Huaizheng's affair ended in failure, people only then understood Dan's far-sighted caution.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huaizheng's affair collapsed in scandal, people understood at last Dan's far-sighted caution.

sentences.zh: 內臣劉承規以忠謹得幸，病且死，求為節度使。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Liu Chenggui, through loyalty and carefulness winning favor, when ill and near death requested to be made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Chenggui had won favor through loyalty and discretion. When he fell gravely ill and faced death, he asked to be made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝語旦曰：「承規待此以瞑目。」

translations.literal: The emperor told Dan: "Chenggui waits for this to close his eyes in peace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Dan, "Chenggui is waiting for this so he may die in peace."

sentences.zh: 旦執不可，曰：「他日將有求為樞密使者，奈何？」

translations.literal: Dan steadfastly refused and said: "In days to come there will be those who request to be Commissioners of Military Affairs—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan firmly refused. "If we grant this," he said, "in time others will ask to be made Commissioners of Military Affairs—what then?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The request was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 自是內臣官不過留後。

translations.literal: From this time forward, inner attendants' offices did not exceed military deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, eunuchs were never appointed above military deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旦為相，賓客滿堂，無敢以私請。

translations.literal: When Dan was chancellor, guests filled the hall, yet none dared make private requests.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan was chancellor, his hall was crowded with guests, yet none dared ask private favors.

sentences.zh: 察可與言及素知名者，數月後，召與語，詢訪四方利病，或使疏其言而獻之。

translations.literal: Those he observed could be spoken with and those of established reputation—after several months he would summon them to talk, inquire into the benefits and harms throughout the four directions, and sometimes have them write out their views and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: Those he judged worth speaking with, or who were already well known—after several months he would summon them, inquire into conditions and grievances throughout the realm, and sometimes have them set down their views in writing for submission.

sentences.zh: 觀才之所長，密籍其名，其人復來，不見也。

translations.literal: Observing where their talents lay, he secretly recorded their names; if such a person came again, he would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When he observed where their talents lay, he secretly noted their names—and if they came again, he would not receive them.

sentences.zh: 每有差除，先密疏四三人姓名以請，所用者帝以筆點之。

translations.literal: Whenever there were appointments, he first secretly memorialized three or four names to request, and of those to be used the emperor would mark with his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever appointments were to be made, he first submitted a secret memorial naming three or four candidates; the emperor would mark his brush beside the one to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 同列不知，爭有所用，惟旦所用，奏入無不可。

translations.literal: His colleagues did not know; each contended to have his own men used, but only those Dan used—when memorials entered, none failed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues knew nothing of this; each pushed his own men, but only Dan's choices—when the memorials went in—never failed to win approval.

sentences.zh: 丁謂以是數毀旦，帝益厚之。

translations.literal: Ding Wei for this reason several times slandered Dan, yet the emperor treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei used this as a pretext to slander Dan repeatedly, yet the emperor only treated Dan all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 故參政李穆子行簡，以將作監丞家居，有賢行，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: The former participating administrator Li Mu's son Xingjian, living at home as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, had virtuous conduct and was promoted to attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingjian, son of the former participating administrator Li Mu, was living at home as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Noted for his virtue, he was promoted to attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 使者不知其宅，真宗命就中書問旦，人始知行簡為旦所薦。

translations.literal: The envoy did not know his residence; Zhenzong ordered inquiry at the Secretariat of Dan, and people only then learned Xingjian had been recommended by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger did not know where he lived. Zhenzong ordered the Secretariat to ask Dan, and only then did people learn that Xingjian had been recommended by Dan.

sentences.zh: 旦凡所薦，皆人未嘗知。

translations.literal: In everything Dan recommended, people had never known.
translations.idiomatic: In every case, Dan's recommendations were ones no one had known he made.

sentences.zh: 旦沒後，史官修《真宗實錄》，得內出奏章，始知朝士多旦所薦云。

translations.literal: After Dan died, when the historiographers compiled the Veritable Records of Zhenzong and obtained memorials issued from within, they first learned that many court gentlemen had been recommended by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: After Dan's death, when the historiographers compiled the Veritable Records of Zhenzong and gained access to memorials issued from within, they learned for the first time how many court officials Dan had recommended.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫張師德兩詣旦門，不得見，意為人所毀，以告向敏中，為從容明之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Opinion Grandee Zhang Shide twice came to Dan's gate and could not gain audience. He suspected he had been slandered by someone and told Xiang Minzhong, who calmly explained matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Opinion Grandee Zhang Shide twice called at Dan's gate without being received. Suspecting someone had slandered him, he confided in Xiang Minzhong, who calmly explained the situation.

sentences.zh: 及議知制誥，旦曰：「可惜張師德。」

translations.literal: When they deliberated on the drafter of edicts post, Dan said: "It is a pity about Zhang Shide."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of drafter of edicts came under discussion, Dan said, "It is a pity about Zhang Shide."

sentences.zh: 敏中問之，旦曰：「累於上前言師德名家子，有士行，不意兩及吾門。

translations.literal: Minzhong asked why. Dan said: "I have repeatedly told His Majesty before that Shide is the son of a great family and has the conduct of a gentleman; I did not expect him twice to come to my gate.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong asked why. Dan said, "I have told His Majesty repeatedly that Shide comes from a great family and has the bearing of a gentleman. I never expected him to call at my gate twice.

sentences.zh: 狀元及第，榮進素定，但當靜以待之爾。

translations.literal: As principal graduate who passed the examinations, honors and advancement are naturally assured—he need only wait quietly for them.
translations.idiomatic: As principal graduate, honors and advancement were already assured for him—he need only wait quietly.

sentences.zh: 若復奔競，使無階而入者當如何也。」

translations.literal: If he again scrambles for advancement, what of those who have no ladder by which to enter?"
translations.idiomatic: If he scrambles for advancement again, what of those who have no way in at all?"

sentences.zh: 敏中啟以師德之意，旦曰：「旦處安得有人敢輕毀人，但師德後進，待我薄爾。」

translations.literal: Minzhong reported Shide's intentions. Dan said: "In Dan's position, how could anyone dare lightly slander others? But Shide is a junior man who treats me too lightly, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong relayed Shide's intentions. Dan said, "In my position, who would dare lightly slander anyone? But Shide is still a junior man—and he has treated me too lightly, that is all."

sentences.zh: 敏中固稱：「適有闕，望公弗遺。」

translations.literal: Minzhong persistently said: "There happens to be a vacancy; I hope you will not overlook him."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong pressed him: "There happens to be a vacancy now—I hope you will not overlook him."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「第緩之，使師德知，聊以戒貪進、激薄俗也。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "Just delay it, so Shide may understand—it will serve to warn against greedy advancement and stir up a base custom."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Just delay it a while, so Shide understands—it will serve to warn against greedy scrambling for office and to rebuke a debased custom."

sentences.zh: 石普知許州不法，朝議欲就劾。

translations.literal: Shi Pu, as prefect of Xuzhou, acted unlawfully; the court deliberated on impeaching him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, as prefect of Xuzhou, had acted unlawfully, and the court deliberated impeaching him in place.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「普武人，不明典憲，恐恃薄效，妄有生事。

translations.literal: Dan said: "Pu is a military man who does not understand statutes and ordinances; I fear he may rely on slight achievements and recklessly stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Pu is a military man who does not understand law and precedent. I fear that, relying on modest service, he may rashly make trouble.

sentences.zh: 必須重行，乞召歸置獄。」

translations.literal: There must be severe punishment; I beg that he be summoned back and placed in prison."
translations.idiomatic: Severe measures are required. I ask that he be recalled and placed in custody."

sentences.zh: 乃下御史按之，一日而獄具。

translations.literal: The censor was thereupon dispatched to investigate; in one day the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The censors were dispatched to investigate, and within a day the case was complete.

sentences.zh: 議者以為不屈國法而保全武臣，真國體也。

translations.literal: Deliberators considered that not yielding on state law yet preserving the military gentleman was truly the substance of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that upholding the law without sacrificing a military officer was true statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 薛奎為江淮發運使，辭旦，旦無他語，但云：「東南民力竭矣。」

translations.literal: Xue Kui, as commissioner for Huai River transport, took leave of Dan. Dan had no other words but said: "The strength of the southeastern people is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kui, upon leaving for his post as commissioner for Huai River transport, called on Dan to take leave. Dan said nothing else but this: "The strength of the people in the southeast is exhausted."

sentences.zh: 奎退而曰：「真宰相之言也。」

translations.literal: Kui withdrew and said: "Truly the words of a chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Kui withdrew and said, "Those are truly a chancellor's words."

sentences.zh: 張士遜為江西轉運使，辭旦求教，旦曰：「朝廷榷利至矣。」

translations.literal: Zhang Shixun, as Jiangxi transport commissioner, took leave of Dan seeking instruction. Dan said: "The court's monopoly profits have reached their limit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shixun, upon leaving for his post as Jiangxi transport commissioner, called on Dan for counsel. Dan said, "The court has already taken monopoly profits as far as they can go."

sentences.zh: 士遜迭更是職，思旦之言，未嘗求利，識者曰：「此運使識大體。」

translations.literal: Shixun, rotating through this office, thought on Dan's words and never sought profit; observers said: "This transport commissioner sees the big picture."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun served in that post in turn, kept Dan's words in mind, and never pressed for more profit. Observers said, "This transport commissioner sees the larger picture."

sentences.zh: 張詠知成都，召還，以任中正代之，言者以為不可。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong governed Chengdu and was recalled; Ren Zhongzheng was appointed to replace him. Memorialists considered this unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong was recalled from governing Chengdu and Ren Zhongzheng was appointed to replace him, critics objected.

sentences.zh: 帝問旦，對曰：「非中正不能守詠之規。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Dan, who answered: "Only Zhongzheng can preserve Yong's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Dan, who answered, "Only Zhongzheng can preserve Yong's policies.

sentences.zh: 他人往，妄有變更矣。」

translations.literal: If another went, there would be reckless changes."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone else were sent, policies would be changed recklessly."

sentences.zh: 李迪、賀邊有時名，舉進士，迪以賦落韻，邊以《當仁不讓於師論》以「師」為「眾」，與注疏異，皆不預。

translations.literal: Li Di and He Bian had reputations of the times. Taking the jinshi examinations, Di failed for a rhyme error in his fu; Bian, in his essay 'On When It Comes to Benevolence One Does Not Defer Even to One's Teacher,' took 'teacher' as 'the multitude,' differing from commentaries and annotations—both were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Di and He Bian were men of contemporary renown. In the jinshi examination Di was rejected for a rhyme fault in his fu; Bian, in his exposition on "When it comes to benevolence, one does not defer even to one's teacher," interpreted "teacher" as "the multitude," at odds with the standard commentaries—both were passed over.

sentences.zh: 主文奏乞收試，旦曰：「迪雖犯不考，然出於不意，其過可略。

translations.literal: The chief examiner memorialized requesting they be admitted to testing. Dan said: "Though Di violated the rule for non-examination, yet it arose unexpectedly—his fault may be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: The chief examiner memorialized asking that they be admitted to examination. Dan said, "Di did violate the rule for disqualification, but it was inadvertent—his fault may be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 邊特立異說，將令後生務為穿鑿，漸不可長。」

translations.literal: Bian alone upheld a divergent doctrine; it would make later students strive for forced interpretations—a trend that must not be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: But Bian deliberately upheld a divergent reading. That would teach younger scholars to pursue forced interpretations—a trend that must not be indulged."

sentences.zh: 遂收迪而黜邊。

translations.literal: Di was thereupon admitted and Bian dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Di was admitted; Bian was rejected.

sentences.zh: 旦任事久，人有謗之者，輒引咎不辨。

translations.literal: Dan served long in office; when people slandered him, he always took blame upon himself without disputing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had served long in office. When people slandered him, he always took the blame upon himself without rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 至人有過失，雖人主盛怒，可辨者辨之，必得而後已。

translations.literal: But when others had faults, even if the sovereign was greatly angered, where defense was possible he defended them and did not stop until success.
translations.idiomatic: But when others had faults—even when the emperor was furious—he defended them where defense was possible, and never stopped until he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 素羸多疾，自東魯復命，連歲求解，優詔褒答，繼以面諭，委任無貳。

translations.literal: He had always been frail and often ill. Returning from reporting on the Eastern tour, year after year he sought release from office; gracious edicts praised and answered him, followed by face-to-face instruction, and his trust and appointment never wavered.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been frail and often ill. After returning from the eastern tour he asked year after year to be relieved; gracious edicts commended him in reply, the emperor reassured him in person, and his trust and appointment never wavered.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，進位太保，為兗州太極觀奉上寶冊使，復加太尉兼侍中，五日一赴起居，入中書，遇軍國重事，不限時日入預參決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was advanced to Grand Guardian, served as envoy presenting the precious register at the Taiji Abbey at Yanzhou, was again given Grand Marshal concurrently with Palace Secretariat Director, attended court every five days, entered the Secretariat, and on encountering weighty military and state affairs entered without limit on time to participate in decisions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianxi era he was promoted to Grand Guardian and appointed envoy to present the precious register at the Taiji Abbey in Yanzhou. He was further made Grand Marshal and Palace Secretariat Director; he attended court every five days, entered the Secretariat, and on weighty military and state matters was summoned to deliberate without regard to the hour.

sentences.zh: 旦愈畏避，上疏懇辭，又托同列奏白。

translations.literal: Dan grew ever more fearful and avoiding; he submitted a memorial earnestly declining, and also had his colleagues memorialize on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Dan grew ever more fearful of office and submitted a memorial earnestly asking to be relieved; he also had his colleagues speak on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝重違其意，止加封邑。

translations.literal: The emperor, greatly reluctant to go against his wish, only added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, loath to go against his wishes, only increased his fief.

sentences.zh: 一日，獨對滋福殿，帝曰：「朕方以大事託卿，而卿疾如此。」

translations.literal: One day, alone facing him in Zifu Hall, the emperor said: "I am just now entrusting you with great affairs, yet your illness is such as this."
translations.idiomatic: One day, granted a private audience in Zifu Hall, the emperor said, "I am entrusting you with weighty affairs, yet your illness is so severe."

sentences.zh: 因命皇太子出拜，旦皇恐走避，太子隨而拜之。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the crown prince to come out and bow; Dan, in panic and fear, fled to avoid it, and the crown prince followed and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the crown prince to come forward and bow. Dan, terrified, tried to flee; the crown prince followed and bowed to him anyway.

sentences.zh: 旦言：「太子盛德，必任陛下事。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "The crown prince possesses great virtue and will surely undertake Your Majesty's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "The crown prince is greatly virtuous and will surely bear Your Majesty's burdens."

sentences.zh: 因薦可為大臣者十餘人，其後不至宰相惟李及、淩策二人，亦為名臣。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended more than ten men who could serve as great ministers; afterward those who did not reach chancellor were only Li Ji and Ling Ce—both also famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended more than ten men fit for high ministerial office. Of these, only Li Ji and Ling Ce never became chancellor—yet both were celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 旦復求避位，帝睹其形瘁，憫然許之。

translations.literal: Dan again sought to avoid his position; the emperor, seeing his wasted form, pityingly consented.
translations.idiomatic: Dan again asked to step aside. Seeing how wasted he had become, the emperor pityingly agreed.

sentences.zh: 以太尉領玉清昭應宮使，給宰相半俸。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Marshal concurrently commissioner of the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace, granted half a chancellor's salary.
translations.idiomatic: He retained the title Grand Marshal and was made commissioner of the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace, with half a chancellor's salary.

sentences.zh: 初，旦以宰相兼使，今罷相，使猶領之，其專置使自旦始焉。

translations.literal: At first Dan had held the commissioner post concurrently with the chancellorship; now, though dismissed as chancellor, he still held the commissioner post—the dedicated commissioner appointment began with Dan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dan had held the commissioner post while serving as chancellor. Now, though he had left the chancellorship, he still held the commissioner post—the dedicated appointment of such commissioners began with Dan.

sentences.zh: 尋又命肩輿入禁，使子雍與直省吏挾扶，見於延和殿。

translations.literal: Soon he was also ordered to enter the forbidden precinct in a sedan chair; his son Yong, together with direct-service clerks, supported him, and he was received in Yanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also permitted to enter the palace precinct in a sedan chair. His son Yong and direct-service clerks supported him, and he was received in Yanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿今疾亟，萬一有不諱，使朕以天下事付之誰乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your illness is now urgent; in the event of the unforeseen, to whom should I entrust affairs under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your illness is now grave. If the unforeseen should happen, to whom should I entrust the affairs of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「知臣莫若君，惟明主擇之。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "No one knows his ministers like the sovereign; let the enlightened ruler choose."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "No one knows his ministers as the sovereign does. Let the enlightened ruler choose."

sentences.zh: 再三問，不對。

translations.literal: Asked again and again, he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Asked again and again, he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 時張詠、馬亮皆為尚書，帝歷問二人，亦不對，因曰：「試以卿意言之。」

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yong and Ma Liang were both vice directors; the emperor asked the two in turn, and they too did not answer. He then said: "Try stating your own view."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Ma Liang were both serving as vice directors of state affairs. The emperor asked them in turn; they too would not answer. He then said, "Tell me your own view."

sentences.zh: 旦強起舉笏曰：「以臣之愚，莫如寇準。」

translations.literal: Dan forcibly roused himself, raised his tablet, and said: "In this subject's foolishness, none is better than Kou Zhun."
translations.idiomatic: Dan forced himself upright, raised his memorial tablet, and said, "In my poor judgment, none is better than Kou Zhun."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「準性剛褊，卿更思其次。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhun's nature is stubborn and narrow; think again for the next choice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhun's nature is stubborn and narrow-minded. Think of the next choice."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「他人，臣所不知也。

translations.literal: Dan said: "As for others, this subject does not know.
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "As for anyone else, I do not know.

sentences.zh: 臣病困，不能久侍。」

translations.literal: This subject's illness is severe; I cannot attend long."
translations.idiomatic: My illness is severe. I cannot stay long."

sentences.zh: 遂辭退。

translations.literal: He thereupon took leave and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後旦沒歲餘，竟用準為相。

translations.literal: More than a year after Dan's death, Zhun was at last employed as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year after Dan's death, Kou Zhun was at last made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 旦疾甚，遣內侍問者日或三四，帝手自和藥，並薯蕷粥賜之。

translations.literal: When Dan's illness was severe, inner attendants sent to inquire came three or four times a day; the emperor personally compounded medicine and also bestowed yam porridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan's illness grew severe, imperial envoys inquired after him three or four times a day. The emperor personally prepared medicine and sent medicinal yam porridge as well.

sentences.zh: 旦與楊億素厚，延至臥內，請撰遺表。

translations.literal: Dan and Yang Yi had long been close; he invited him to his sickbed and requested he draft his testament memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Yang Yi had long been close. He had Yi come to his sickbed and asked him to draft his death memorial.

sentences.zh: 且言：「忝為宰輔，不可以將盡之言，為宗親求官，止敘生平遭遇，願日親庶政，進用賢士，少減焦勞之意。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Having been disgracefully a chief minister, I cannot in words near death seek offices for kinsmen—only narrate encounters in life's course, express the wish to attend closely to everyday governance daily, advance and employ worthy gentlemen, and reduce somewhat the burden of anxious toil."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Having disgracefully served as chief minister, I cannot use my last words to seek offices for kinsmen. Let it only recount my life's course, express the wish that Your Majesty attend closely to everyday governance, advance worthy men, and lighten somewhat the burden of your anxious toil."

sentences.zh: 仍戒子弟：「我家盛名清德，當務儉素，保守門風，不得事於泰侈，勿為厚葬以金寶置柩中。」

translations.literal: He also admonished his sons and nephews: "Our house has famous repute and pure virtue—you must practice simplicity and frugality, preserve the family tradition, must not indulge in excessive luxury, and must not bury lavishly with gold and jewels placed in the coffin."
translations.idiomatic: He also admonished his sons and nephews: "Our house bears a famous name and spotless reputation. Be sparing and plain, preserve the family tradition, indulge in no extravagance, and do not give me a lavish burial with gold and jewels placed in the coffin."

sentences.zh: 表上，真宗歎之，遂幸其第，賜白金五千兩。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Zhenzong sighed over it, then visited his residence and bestowed five thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Zhenzong sighed over it, visited Dan's residence in person, and bestowed five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 旦作奏辭之，槁末，自益四句云：「益懼多藏，況無所用，見欲散施，以息咎殃。」

translations.literal: Dan wrote a memorial declining it; at the end of the draft he himself added four lines saying: "I fear all the more hoarding abundance, and moreover have no use for it; seeing this, I wish to distribute it in charity, to still blame and misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Dan wrote a memorial declining the gift. At the end of the draft he added four lines of his own: "I fear hoarding wealth all the more, and have no use for it besides. I wish to distribute it in charity, to avert blame and misfortune."

sentences.zh: 即舁至內闥，詔不許。

translations.literal: It was immediately carried to the inner gate; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: It was carried at once to the inner palace gate; an edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 還至門，旦已薨，年六十一。

translations.literal: When they returned to the gate, Dan had already died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When the bearers returned to his gate, Dan had already died, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝臨其喪慟，廢朝三日，贈太師、尚書令、魏國公，諡文正，又別次發哀。

translations.literal: The emperor attended his mourning in grief, canceled court for three days, granted posthumously Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, with posthumous name Wen Zheng, and also held a separate session of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his mourning in grief, canceled court for three days, and posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Wen Zheng. He also held a separate session of mourning.

sentences.zh: 後數日，張旻赴鎮河陽，例宜飲餞，以旦故，不舉樂。

translations.literal: Several days later, Zhang Min departed to his post at Heyang; by precedent a farewell feast should have been held, but because of Dan no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Zhang Min departed to take up his post at Heyang. By precedent a farewell feast should have been held with music, but because of Dan none was performed.

sentences.zh: 錄其子、弟、侄、外孫、門客、常從，授官者十數人。

translations.literal: His sons, younger brothers, nephews, grandsons by daughters, retained clients, and regular attendants were enrolled; more than ten were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, brothers, nephews, grandsons by daughters, retained clients, and regular attendants were enrolled—more than ten were granted office.

sentences.zh: 諸子服除，又各進一官。

translations.literal: When his sons' mourning periods ended, each was again advanced one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons' mourning periods ended, each was again promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 已而聞旦奏槁自益四句，取視，泣下久之。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing of the four lines Dan had added to his memorial draft, the emperor took it to view and wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor heard of the four lines Dan had added to his memorial draft. He took it up to read and wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 旦有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Dan had a collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan left collected writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，詔配享真宗廟廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing, an edict granted him a place in Zhenzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianxing era, an edict granted him a place among those enshrined in Emperor Zhenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 及建碑，仁宗篆其首曰「全德元老之碑」。

translations.literal: When a stele was erected, Renzong wrote its head in seal script: 'Stele of the Elder of Complete Virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: When a stele was erected, Renzong inscribed its head in seal script: "Stele of the Elder of Complete Virtue."

sentences.zh: 旦事寡嫂有禮，與弟旭友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: Dan served his widowed sister-in-law with propriety and was deeply affectionate with his younger brother Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan treated his widowed sister-in-law with full propriety and was deeply affectionate with his younger brother Xu.

sentences.zh: 婚姻不求門閥。

translations.literal: In marriage he did not seek high pedigrees.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage he did not seek great pedigrees.

sentences.zh: 被服質素，家人欲以繒錦飾氈席，不許。

translations.literal: His dress was plain and simple; when family members wished to adorn felt mats with silks and brocades, he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: His dress was plain and simple. When members of his household wished to trim felt mats with silks and brocades, he forbade it.

sentences.zh: 有貨玉帶者，弟以為佳，呈旦，旦命係之，曰：「還見佳否？」

translations.literal: Someone was selling a jade belt; his younger brother thought it fine and presented it to Dan. Dan ordered it tied on and said: "Can you still see whether it is fine?"
translations.idiomatic: A merchant was selling a jade belt. His younger brother thought it fine and showed it to Dan. Dan had it strapped on and said, "Can you still tell whether it looks fine?"

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「係之安得自見？」

translations.literal: His younger brother said: "Once it is tied on, how can one see it oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: His brother said, "Once it's strapped on, how can you see it yourself?"

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「自負重而使觀者稱好，無乃勞乎！」

translations.literal: Dan said: "To bear the weight oneself yet make onlookers call it fine—is that not laborious!"
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "To burden yourself and yet make onlookers praise it—is that not a pointless strain?"

sentences.zh: 亟還之。

translations.literal: He immediately returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent it back at once.

sentences.zh: 故所服止於賜帶。

translations.literal: Therefore what he wore was limited to the bestowed belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he wore nothing beyond the belt the emperor had granted him.

sentences.zh: 家人未嘗見其怒，飲食不精潔，但不食而已。

translations.literal: His family never saw him angry; when food was not refined and clean, he simply would not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: His household never saw him lose his temper. When food was not properly prepared, he simply refused to eat it.

sentences.zh: 嘗試以少埃墨投羹中，旦惟啖飯，問何不啜羹，則曰：「我偶不喜肉。」

translations.literal: Once they tried putting a little soot and ink into the soup; Dan ate only rice. When asked why he did not drink the soup, he said: "I happen not to like meat."
translations.idiomatic: Once the household tested him by dropping a bit of soot into the soup. Dan ate only the rice. Asked why he would not touch the soup, he said, "I happen not to care for meat."

sentences.zh: 後又墨其飯，則曰：「吾今日不喜飯，可別具粥。」

translations.literal: Later they again soiled his rice, and he said: "Today I do not care for rice—prepare some congee separately."
translations.idiomatic: Later they dirtied his rice as well. He said, "I am not in the mood for rice today. Bring me some congee instead."

sentences.zh: 旦不置田宅，曰：「子孫當各念自立，何必田宅，徒使爭財為不義爾。」

translations.literal: Dan did not acquire fields and houses, saying: "My descendants should each think of standing on their own—why need fields and houses? They would only make them fight over wealth in unrighteous ways."
translations.idiomatic: Dan never bought land or property. He said, "My descendants should each learn to stand on their own. Why leave them fields and houses, only to drive them into squabbling over money?"

sentences.zh: 真宗以其所居陋，欲治之，旦辭以先人舊廬，乃止。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong found his dwelling shabby and wished to renovate it, Dan declined on the grounds that it was his forefathers' old residence, and the emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong found his home too modest and offered to rebuild it, Dan declined, saying it was his ancestors' old house—and the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 宅門壞，主者徹新之，暫於廡下啟側門出入。

translations.literal: When the house gate was damaged, the steward dismantled it to replace it with a new one, and for a time opened a side gate under the corridor for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: When the main gate fell into disrepair, the steward took it down to rebuild it, and Dan entered and left for a time through a side door under the eaves.

sentences.zh: 旦至側門，據鞍俯過，門成復由之，皆不問焉。

translations.literal: When Dan reached the side gate, he leaned over the saddle to pass through; when the main gate was finished he still used the side gate—and never inquired about any of it.
translations.idiomatic: At the side gate he would lean from the saddle to slip through; even after the main gate was restored he kept using the side entrance—and never asked a word about any of it.

sentences.zh: 三子：雍，國子博士；

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yong, Director of the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yong, who was a director at the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 冲，左贊善大夫；

translations.literal: Chong, Left Supporter of Goodness Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Left Supporter of Goodness Grandee;

sentences.zh: 素，別有傳。

translations.literal: Su—treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Su, who has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 向敏中

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong

sentences.zh: 向敏中，字常之，開封人。

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong, courtesy name Changzhi, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong, styled Changzhi, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父瑀，仕漢符離令。

translations.literal: His father Yu served Han as magistrate of Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as magistrate of Fuli under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 性嚴毅，惟敏中一子，躬自教督，不假顏色。

translations.literal: In nature stern and resolute, he had only Minzhong as a son and personally taught and supervised him, never softening his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and unyielding by nature, he had only Minzhong as a son. He tutored the boy himself and never eased his stern manner.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂其母曰：「大吾門者，此兒也。」

translations.literal: He once told his wife: "The one who will enlarge our house is this boy."
translations.idiomatic: He once told his wife, "This boy will be the one to bring honor to our house."

sentences.zh: 敏中隨瑀赴調京師，有書生過門，見敏中，謂鄰母曰：「此兒風骨秀異，貴且壽。」

translations.literal: When Minzhong followed Yu to the capital for his posting, a scholar passed the gate, saw Minzhong, and said to a neighboring woman: "This boy's bearing is exceptional—he will be noble and long-lived."
translations.idiomatic: When Minzhong accompanied Yu to the capital for his assignment, a scholar passing the gate saw the boy and told a neighbor, "This child has an extraordinary presence. He will rise high and live long."

sentences.zh: 鄰母入告其家，比出，已不見矣。

translations.literal: The neighboring woman went in to tell the family; by the time they came out, he was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor went in to tell the family, but by the time they came out, the scholar had vanished.

sentences.zh: 及冠，繼丁內外憂，能刻厲自立，有大志，不屑貧窶。

translations.literal: Upon reaching adulthood he successively mourned the deaths of both parents, was able to discipline himself and stand on his own, had great ambition, and disdained poverty and want.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he lost both parents in succession. He disciplined himself, refused to be beaten down by hardship, nursed large ambitions, and would not be humbled by poverty.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年進士，解褐將作監丞、通判吉州，就改右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, upon first appointment became Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and vice-prefect of Jizhou, and was thereupon promoted to Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he took the jinshi degree, entered service as Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction and vice-prefect of Jizhou, and was then made Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee.

sentences.zh: 轉運使張齊賢薦其材，代還，為著作郎。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Zhang Qixian recommended his talent; when his term ended and he returned, he was made Compiler in the Institute of Literary Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Zhang Qixian recommended his ability, and when Minzhong's tour ended and he returned to court he was appointed Compiler in the Institute of Literary Compilation.

sentences.zh: 召見便殿，占對明暢，太宗善之，命為戶部推官，出為淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Easy Rest, his impromptu responses were clear and fluent; Taizong was pleased and appointed him investigating censor in the Ministry of Revenue, then sent him out as vice transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Easy Rest, he answered with clarity and ease. Taizong was impressed and made him investigating censor in the Ministry of Revenue, then sent him out as vice transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時領外計者，皆以權寵自尊，所至畏憚，敏中不尚威察，待僚屬有禮，勤於勸勖，職務修舉。

translations.literal: At that time those who headed external fiscal administration all relied on power and favor to magnify themselves, and wherever they went people feared them; Minzhong did not emphasize intimidating inspection, treated subordinates with courtesy, diligently encouraged them, and his duties were fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal officials in the provinces at that time often lorded their power and imperial favor over others, and everywhere they went people were afraid of them. Minzhong did not rule by intimidation. He treated his staff with courtesy, worked hard to encourage them, and brought every duty to completion.

sentences.zh: 或薦其有武幹者，召入，將授諸司副使。

translations.literal: When someone recommended him as having military competence, he was summoned in and was about to be appointed deputy commissioner of one of the bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When someone recommended him for military talent, he was recalled to court and was to be appointed deputy commissioner of one of the military bureaus.

sentences.zh: 敏中懇辭，仍獻所著文，加直史館，遣還任。

translations.literal: Minzhong earnestly declined, and moreover submitted writings he had composed; he was given concurrent appointment as rectifier in the History Institute and sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong pleaded to be excused and submitted his own writings instead. He was given a concurrent post as rectifier in the History Institute and sent back to his former assignment.

sentences.zh: 以耕籍恩，超左司諫，入為戶部判官、知制誥。

translations.literal: By grace of the plowing-and-altar ceremony, he was leap-promoted to Left Remonstrance of the Left Office, entered the capital as chief judge of the Ministry of Revenue and draft drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of the plowing-and-altar grace he was leap-promoted to Left Remonstrance of the Left Office, then brought into court as chief judge of the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，權判大理寺。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned to ad hoc supervision of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was placed in charge of the Court of Judicial Review on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 時沒入祖吉贓錢，分賜法吏，敏中引鍾離意委珠事，獨不受。

translations.literal: At the time confiscated bribe money from Zu Ji was divided and bestowed on legal officials; Minzhong cited Zhong Li Yi's story of casting away pearls and alone refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the time confiscated bribe money from Zu Ji was being distributed among the legal officials. Minzhong cited Zhongli Yi's refusal of pearls and alone declined his share.

sentences.zh: 妖尼道安構獄，事連開封判官張去華，敏中妻父也，以故得請不預決讞。

translations.literal: The sorceress-nun Dao'an fabricated a case that implicated Kaifeng judge Zhang Quhua—Minzhong's father-in-law—wherefore he obtained permission not to participate in the trial and sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: The sorceress-nun Dao'an engineered a false case that touched Kaifeng judge Zhang Quhua, Minzhong's father-in-law. On that account he obtained permission to recuse himself from the trial.

sentences.zh: 既而法官皆貶，猶以親累落職，出知廣州。

translations.literal: In the end the legal officials were all demoted; he still, through kinship involvement, lost his post and was sent out as prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the end every official involved in the case was demoted. Even so, Minzhong was dislodged from office through his family tie and sent out as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，面敘其事，太宗為之感動，許以不三歲召還。

translations.literal: On entering to take leave he narrated the affair to the emperor's face; Taizong was moved and promised to recall him within three years.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave he laid out the whole affair before the emperor. Taizong was deeply moved and promised to recall him within three years.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遷職方員外郎，遣之。

translations.literal: The next day he was transferred to External Affairs Assistant in the Ministry of Personnel and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was promoted to External Affairs Assistant in the Ministry of Personnel and sent on his way.

sentences.zh: 是州兼掌市舶，前守多涉譏議。

translations.literal: That prefecture also administered the maritime trade office; previous prefects had mostly been involved in criticism and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou also supervised the maritime trade office, and many of Minzhong's predecessors had been tainted by scandal.

sentences.zh: 敏中至荊南，預市藥物以往，在任無所須，以清廉聞。

translations.literal: Minzhong reached Jingnan, purchased medicines in advance to take with him, needed nothing while in office, and became known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: On his way south Minzhong stopped at Jingnan to buy medicines for the journey. Once in office he accepted nothing from anyone and won a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 就擢廣南東路轉運使，召為工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to transport commissioner of the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan, then summoned as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to transport commissioner of the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan, then recalled to court as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 太宗飛白書敏中洎張詠二名付中書，曰：「此二人，名臣也，朕將用之。」

translations.literal: Taizong wrote the names of Minzhong and Zhang Yong in feibai script and handed them to the Chief Council, saying: "These two men are famed ministers; I intend to employ them."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote Minzhong's name and Zhang Yong's in flying-white script and sent the list to the Chief Council. "These two," he said, "are ministers of proven worth. I mean to use them."

sentences.zh: 左右因稱其材，並命為樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Those around him thereupon praised their talents, and both were appointed as direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants then spoke up for their abilities, and both men were appointed direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時通進銀臺司主出納書奏，領於樞密院，頗多壅遏，或至漏失。

translations.literal: At that time the Directorate for Transmission of Documents handled receipt and dispatch of memorials, was overseen by the Bureau of Military Affairs, and often had much blockage and delay, sometimes even losses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Directorate for Transmission of Documents, which handled incoming and outgoing memorials under the Bureau of Military Affairs, was badly clogged—documents were delayed and sometimes lost altogether.

sentences.zh: 敏中具奏其事，恐遠方有失事機，請別置局，命官專蒞，校其簿籍，詔命敏中與詠領其局。

translations.literal: Minzhong fully memorialized on the matter, fearing that distant regions might miss critical opportunities; he requested that a separate office be established with designated officials in charge to check the registers—and an edict ordered Minzhong and Yong to head the office.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong memorialized on the problem in full, warning that distant provinces might miss urgent business. He proposed a separate office with dedicated officials to keep the registers in order. An edict put Minzhong and Yong in charge.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲大任敏中，當途者忌之。

translations.literal: Taizong wished to give Minzhong a great appointment; those in power were jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong meant to give Minzhong a major appointment, but men at the top were jealous of him.

sentences.zh: 會有言敏中在法寺時，皇甫侃監無為軍榷務，以賄敗，發書歷詣朝貴求為末減，敏中亦受之。

translations.literal: It happened that someone said that when Minzhong was at the Court of Judicial Review, Huangfu Kan, supervising the salt monopoly at Wuwei Army, failed through bribery and sent letters going around to court nobles seeking leniency—and Minzhong too had received one.
translations.idiomatic: Just then word spread that while Minzhong was at the Court of Judicial Review, Huangfu Kan, who supervised the salt monopoly at Wuwei Army, had been ruined by bribery and had sent letters to one court grandee after another begging for leniency—and that Minzhong too had received one.

sentences.zh: 事下御史，按實嘗有書及門，敏中睹其名，不啟封遣去。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the censorate; investigation confirmed that a letter had indeed reached his gate—Minzhong saw the name, did not break the seal, and sent it back.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the censorate. Investigation confirmed that a letter had reached his door. Minzhong saw Huangfu Kan's name on the seal, never opened it, and sent it back unopened.

sentences.zh: 俄捕得侃私僮詰之，云其書尋納筒中，瘞臨江傳舍。

translations.literal: Soon Kan's private servant was captured and interrogated; he said the letter had soon been put into a tube and buried at a post station on the Lin River.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Kan's personal servant was seized and questioned. He said the letter had been placed in a tube and buried at an inn on the Lin River.

sentences.zh: 馳驛掘得，封題如故。

translations.literal: By express courier they dug it up and found the seal and inscription intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: A courier was dispatched at once. They dug it up, and the seal and address were still intact.

sentences.zh: 太宗大驚異，召見，慰諭賞激，遂決於登用。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly astonished, summoned him to audience, consoled and praised and encouraged him, and thereupon resolved to promote him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was astonished. He summoned Minzhong, comforted and praised him, and from that moment decided to advance him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜右諫議大夫、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Remonstrance Recipient and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Remonstrance Recipient and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 自郎中至是百餘日，超擢如此。

translations.literal: From bureau director to this post was a little over a hundred days—such was the leap in promotion.
translations.idiomatic: From bureau director to this post was barely a hundred days—a promotion as sudden as it was steep.

sentences.zh: 時西北用兵，樞機之任，專主謀議，敏中明辨有才略，遇事敏速，凡二邊道路、斥堠、走集之所，莫不周知。

translations.literal: At that time war was being waged in the northwest; the burden of the bureau lay chiefly in planning. Minzhong was clear-sighted and resourceful, swift in handling affairs; every route on both frontiers, every beacon and gathering place, he knew thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: War was then underway in the northwest, and the Bureau of Military Affairs bore the chief burden of planning. Minzhong was clear-minded and able, quick when action was needed. He knew every road on both frontiers, every beacon and staging point, down to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 至道初，遷給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era he was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhidao era he was made Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，敏中適在疾告，力起，見於東序，即遣視事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded to the throne, Minzhong happened to be on leave for illness; he forced himself to rise, was received in the eastern wing, and was immediately sent back to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Minzhong happened to be on sick leave. He forced himself to rise, was received in the eastern wing, and at once returned to office.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會曹彬為樞密使，改為副使。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin became Privy Councillor, Minzhong was changed to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin became Privy Councillor, Minzhong was made vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，拜兵部侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was appointed Vice Minister of War and participation councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping era he was appointed Vice Minister of War and participation councilor.

sentences.zh: 從幸大名，屬宋湜病，代兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on the visit to Daming, when Song Mi fell ill Minzhong acted in his stead as concurrent commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Daming, when Song Mi fell ill Minzhong acted in his stead as concurrent commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時大兵之後，議遣重臣慰撫邊郡，命為河北、河東安撫大使，以陳堯叟、馮拯為副，發禁兵萬人翼從。

translations.literal: At that time, after major campaigns, the court discussed sending a high minister to comfort and pacify the frontier prefectures; he was appointed Pacification Commissioner-General for Hebei and Hedong, with Chen Yaosou and Feng Zheng as deputies, and ten thousand imperial guards were dispatched to escort him.
