translations.idiomatic: After major campaigns, the court discussed sending a senior minister to comfort and pacify the frontier prefectures. Minzhong was appointed Pacification Commissioner-General for Hebei and Hedong, with Chen Yaosou and Feng Zheng as deputies, and ten thousand imperial guards were sent to escort him.

sentences.zh: 所至訪民疾苦，宴犒官吏，莫不感悅。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he inquired into the people's hardships, feasted and rewarded officials, and all were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he inquired into the people's hardships, feasted and rewarded officials, and all were moved and pleased.

sentences.zh: 四年，以本官同平章事，充集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with his existing rank he was made Associate Grand Counselor and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, at his existing rank he was made Associate Grand Counselor and grand academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 故相薛居正孫安上不肖，其居第有詔無得貿易，敏中違詔質之。

translations.literal: Former chancellor Xue Juzheng's grandson Anshang was unworthy; an edict forbade trade in his residence, yet Minzhong violated the edict and took it in pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Juzheng's grandson Anshang was a ne'er-do-well. An edict forbade the sale of his grandfather's house, yet Minzhong took it in pledge in defiance of the order.

sentences.zh: 會居正子惟吉嫠婦柴將攜貲產適張齊賢，安上訴其事，柴遂言敏中嘗求娶己，不許，以是陰庇安上。

translations.literal: It happened that Juzheng's son Weiji's widowed daughter-in-law Chai was about to take her assets and marry Zhang Qixian; Anshang sued over the matter, and Chai then said Minzhong had once sought to marry her, was refused, and on that account secretly shielded Anshang.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's daughter-in-law Chai, a widow, was about to remarry Zhang Qixian and take her assets with her. Anshang brought suit, and Chai then claimed that Minzhong had once asked to marry her, had been refused, and was secretly protecting Anshang out of spite.

sentences.zh: 真宗以問敏中，敏中言近喪妻不復議婚，未嘗求婚於柴，真宗因不復問。

translations.literal: Zhenzong questioned Minzhong about it; Minzhong said he had recently lost his wife and was no longer considering marriage, and had never proposed to Chai—and Zhenzong therefore asked no more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong questioned Minzhong, who replied that he had recently lost his wife, was not contemplating remarriage, and had never proposed to Chai. The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 柴又伐鼓，訟益急，遂下御史臺，並得敏中質宅之狀。

translations.literal: Chai again beat the drum of appeal, her lawsuit grew more urgent, and the matter was referred to the censorate—which also obtained evidence of Minzhong's pledging of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Chai beat the appeal drum again, pressing her case harder. The matter went to the censorate, which also turned up proof of Minzhong's pledge on the house.

sentences.zh: 時王嗣宗為鹽鐵使，素忌敏中，因對，言敏中議娶王承衍女弟，密約已定而未納采。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Cizong was salt and iron commissioner and had long resented Minzhong; taking advantage of an audience he said Minzhong had agreed to marry Wang Chengyan's younger sister—the secret pact was set though betrothal gifts had not yet been sent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cizong, commissioner of salt and iron, had long resented Minzhong. Seizing an audience he claimed Minzhong had agreed to marry Wang Chengyan's younger sister—a secret understanding already fixed though the formal betrothal had not yet been sent.

sentences.zh: 真宗詢於王氏，得其實，以敏中前言為妄，罷為戶部侍郎，出知永興軍。

translations.literal: Zhenzong inquired of the Wang family, learned the truth, took Minzhong's earlier words as false, removed him from his bureau post, made him vice minister of revenue, and sent him out as military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong checked with the Wang family and found it true. He judged Minzhong's earlier denial a lie, stripped him of his bureau post, made him vice minister of revenue, and sent him out to command Yongxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 景德初，復兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era he was restored as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingde era he was restored to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 夏州李繼遷兵敗，為潘羅支射傷，自度孤危且死，屬其子德明必歸宋，曰：「一表不聽則再請，雖累百表，不得，請勿止也。」

translations.literal: Li Jiqian of Xia Prefecture was defeated in battle and wounded by Pan Luozhi's arrow; judging himself isolated, imperiled, and near death, he charged his son Deming that he must submit to Song, saying: "If one memorial is not heeded, petition again; even if a hundred memorials are sent and none succeeds, do not cease petitioning."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqian of Xia Prefecture was defeated and wounded by an arrow from Pan Luozhi. Believing himself isolated and near death, he charged his son Deming to submit to Song. "If one petition is refused, send another," he said. "Even if you must send a hundred and still fail, do not stop."

sentences.zh: 繼遷卒，德明納款，就命敏中為鄜延路緣邊安撫使，俄還京兆。

translations.literal: Jiqian died; Deming submitted in good faith; Minzhong was immediately appointed frontier pacification commissioner of the Bian-Yan Circuit, and soon returned to govern Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian died. When Deming offered submission, Minzhong was appointed frontier pacification commissioner of the Bian-Yan Circuit; soon afterward he was put in charge of Jingzhao as well.

sentences.zh: 是冬，真宗幸澶淵，賜敏中密詔，盡付西鄙，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: That winter Zhenzong traveled to Chanyuan and bestowed on Minzhong a secret edict, entrusting the entire western frontier to him and permitting discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Zhenzong went to Chanyuan, he gave Minzhong a secret edict placing the whole western frontier in his hands and authorizing him to act on his own judgment.

sentences.zh: 敏中得詔藏之，視政如常日。

translations.literal: Minzhong received the edict and hid it, conducting administration as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong tucked the edict away and governed exactly as on any other day.

sentences.zh: 會大儺，有告禁卒欲倚儺為亂者，敏中密使麾兵被甲伏廡下幕中。

translations.literal: It happened that during the great nuo exorcism rite someone reported that garrison soldiers intended to use the rite as cover for a revolt; Minzhong secretly had commanders arm troops and hide them under curtains along the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: During the great nuo exorcism someone reported that garrison troops meant to use the festival as cover for a mutiny. Minzhong secretly ordered soldiers under arms to conceal themselves behind curtains along the corridor.

sentences.zh: 明日，盡召賓僚兵官，置酒縱閱，無一人預知者。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned all guests, staff, and military officers, set out wine, and let them watch freely—not one person had foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned every guest, staff member, and officer, set out wine, and let the revelry run freely—not one of them knew what was coming.

sentences.zh: 命儺入，先馳騁於中門外，後召至階，敏中振袂一揮，伏出，盡擒之，果各懷短刃，即席斬焉。

translations.literal: He ordered the nuo performers to enter, first galloping outside the middle gate, then summoned to the steps; Minzhong shook his sleeve and waved—those in ambush rushed out and seized them all; indeed each carried a short blade, and they were beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He had the nuo troupe enter, galloping first outside the middle gate and then called up to the steps. Minzhong swept his sleeve—a signal—and the hidden troops burst out and seized them all. Each man carried a short blade; they were beheaded where they sat.

sentences.zh: 既屏其屍，以灰沙掃庭，張樂宴飲，坐客皆股慄，邊藩遂安。

translations.literal: After the corpses were removed, he swept the courtyard with ash and sand, spread music, and continued the banquet and drinking—the seated guests all trembled in their thighs, and the frontier post was thereafter secure.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bodies were cleared away he had the courtyard swept with ash and sand, the music struck up again, and the feast resumed. Every guest's legs were shaking—but the frontier was secure from that day on.

sentences.zh: 時舊相出鎮，不以軍事為意。

translations.literal: At that time former chancellors sent out to command circuits did not take military affairs to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Former chancellors posted to the provinces at that time rarely took military affairs seriously.

sentences.zh: 寇準雖有重名，所至終日遊宴，則以所愛伶人或付富室，輒厚有得。

translations.literal: Though Kou Zhun enjoyed great renown, wherever he went he spent the whole day feasting and touring, and would lend out beloved performers to wealthy households—for which he always received hefty returns.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun, for all his great reputation, spent his days feasting wherever he was posted, and would lend his favorite performers to rich households—for which he always collected a handsome fee.

sentences.zh: 張齊賢倜儻任情，獲劫盜或至縱遣。

translations.literal: Zhang Qixian was free-spirited and followed his own inclinations; when he captured robbers he sometimes even released them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qixian was free-spirited and indulged his whims—when he caught bandits he sometimes let them go altogether.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，稱敏中曰：「大臣出臨四方，惟敏中盡心於民事爾。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he praised Minzhong, saying: "When great ministers go out to oversee the four quarters, only Minzhong devotes himself wholeheartedly to the people's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he said of Minzhong, "Of all the great ministers sent out to govern the provinces, only Minzhong has truly attended to the people's business."

sentences.zh: 於是有復用之意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had the intention of reemploying him.
translations.idiomatic: After that the emperor began to think of bringing him back.

sentences.zh: 二年，又以德明誓約未定，徙敏中為鄜延路都部署兼知延州，委以經略，改知河南府兼西京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year, because Deming's sworn pledge was not yet settled, Minzhong was transferred to grand deployment commissioner of the Bian-Yan Circuit concurrently prefect of Yanzhou, entrusted with frontier strategy, then changed to prefect of Henan and concurrent defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, with Deming's pledge still unsettled, Minzhong was moved to grand deployment commissioner of the Bian-Yan Circuit and prefect of Yanzhou, with full authority over frontier strategy—then transferred to prefect of Henan and defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，議封泰山，以敏中舊德有人望，召入，權東京留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the feng rite on Mount Tai was under discussion, because Minzhong's old virtue commanded public respect he was summoned in and placed in charge as acting defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dazhong Xiangfu, when Mount Tai feng rites were under discussion, Minzhong's old standing and public regard brought him back to court as acting defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 禮成，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When the rite was completed he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was complete he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時吏部選人多稽滯者，命敏中與溫仲舒領其事。

translations.literal: At that time many candidates in the Ministry of Personnel selections were long delayed; Minzhong and Wen Zhongshu were ordered to take charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Many candidates in the Ministry of Personnel roster were then badly backlogged. Minzhong and Wen Zhongshu were put in charge of clearing the lists.

sentences.zh: 俄兼秘書監，又領工部尚書，充資政殿大學士，賜御詩褒寵。

translations.literal: Soon he was given concurrent appointment as Director of the Palace Library, then also headed the Ministry of Works, was made grand academician of the Hall of Governance Assistance, and was granted an imperial poem in praise and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the Palace Library as well, then the Ministry of Works, was made grand academician of the Hall of Governance Assistance, and received an imperial poem of praise.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，復為留守。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were performed at Fenyin he again served as defender.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sacrificed at Fenyin he again served as defender of the capital.

sentences.zh: 敏中以厚重鎮靜，人情帖然，帝作詩遣使馳賜之。

translations.literal: Minzhong by his weighty steadiness kept popular sentiment settled; the emperor composed a poem and sent an envoy at full speed to bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong's weight and calm kept the populace at ease. The emperor wrote a poem and dispatched a courier at once to present it to him.

sentences.zh: 拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 五年，復拜同平章事，充集賢殿大學士，加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again appointed Associate Grand Counselor, made grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and given the additional title of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again made Associate Grand Counselor, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋充景靈宮使，宮成，進兵部尚書，為兗州景靈宮慶成使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made commissioner of the Jingling Palace; when the palace was completed he was promoted to Minister of War and made celebration commissioner for the Jingling Palace at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commissioner of the Jingling Palace. When the palace was finished he was promoted to Minister of War and named celebration commissioner for the Jingling Palace at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，加吏部尚書，又為應天院奉安太祖聖容禮儀使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was given the additional title of Minister of Personnel, and again served as protocol commissioner for installing the sacred portrait of Taizu at the Hall of Corresponding Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianxi he was made Minister of Personnel and protocol commissioner for installing Taizu's sacred portrait at the Hall of Corresponding Heaven.

sentences.zh: 進右僕射兼門下侍郎，監修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and put in charge of compiling the National History.

sentences.zh: 是日，翰林學士李宗諤當對，帝曰：「朕自即位，未嘗除僕射，今命敏中，此殊命也，敏中應甚喜。」

translations.literal: That day Hanlin Academician Li Zong'e was scheduled for audience; the emperor said: "Since I ascended the throne I have never appointed a vice director; now appointing Minzhong—this is an extraordinary appointment. Minzhong should be very pleased."
translations.idiomatic: That day Hanlin Academician Li Zong'e was on duty for audience. The emperor said, "Since my accession I have never appointed a vice director. To give that rank to Minzhong is an extraordinary honor. He must be delighted."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「敏中今日賀客必多，卿往觀之，勿言朕意也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Today Minzhong's congratulatory visitors must be many—go observe, but do not speak of my intent."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Minzhong's house must be swarming with well-wishers today. Go and see—but say nothing of my purpose."

sentences.zh: 宗諤既至，敏中謝客，門闌寂然。

translations.literal: When Zong'e arrived, Minzhong had turned away visitors; the gate was utterly silent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong'e arrived, Minzhong had declined all callers. The gate was utterly quiet.

sentences.zh: 宗諤與其親徑入，徐賀曰：「今日聞降麻，士大夫莫不歡慰相慶。」

translations.literal: Zong'e entered directly with his close associates and slowly offered congratulations, saying: "Today upon hearing the edict promulgated, no scholar-official has failed to rejoice and congratulate one another."
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e went in with his intimates and offered his congratulations at leisure. "Word of today's appointment has spread," he said. "Every official in the capital is rejoicing."

sentences.zh: 敏中但唯唯。

translations.literal: Minzhong only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong murmured noncommittal replies.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自上即位，未嘗除端揆，非勳德隆重，眷倚殊越，何以至此。」

translations.literal: He again said: "Since the emperor's accession there has never been an appointment to the summit of state—unless one's merit and virtue were profound and imperial favor extraordinarily surpassing, how could one reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e pressed on: "Since Your Majesty's accession no one has been raised to the chief ministership. Without uncommon merit and extraordinary favor, how could anyone reach such a height?"

sentences.zh: 敏中復唯唯。

translations.literal: Minzhong again murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong again murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 又歷陳前世為僕射者勳德禮命之重，敏中亦唯唯，卒無一言。

translations.literal: Again he enumerated in detail the merit, virtue, and weight of investiture of former vice directors; Minzhong also murmured assent, and in the end spoke not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e went on at length about the merit and ceremonial weight that had attended every past vice director. Minzhong murmured along and in the end said not a word.

sentences.zh: 既退，使人問庖中，今日有親賓飲宴否，亦無一人。

translations.literal: After he withdrew he sent someone to ask the kitchen whether there had been any family or guest feasting today—and there was not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: When he withdrew he sent someone to the kitchen to ask whether any relatives or guests had been entertained that day. There had been none.

sentences.zh: 明日，具以所見對。

translations.literal: The next day he fully reported what he had seen in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reported everything he had seen.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「向敏中大耐官職。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xiang Minzhong can truly bear high office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xiang Minzhong has a constitution made for high office."

sentences.zh: 徙玉清昭應宮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner of the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Jade Pure Manifest Response Palace.

sentences.zh: 以年老，累請致政，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Because of old age he repeatedly requested retirement; gracious edicts refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Age pressed upon him and he repeatedly asked to retire, but gracious edicts each time refused.

sentences.zh: 三年重陽，宴苑中，暮歸中風眩，郊祀不任陪從。

translations.literal: In the third year on the Double Ninth Festival, after feasting in the garden he returned at dusk stricken with wind dizziness and was unable to accompany the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In his third year in office, after the Double Ninth feast in the imperial garden he came home at dusk stricken with vertigo and was unable to attend the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 進左僕射、昭文館大學士，奉表懇讓，又表求解，皆不許。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and grand academician of the Hall of Splendid Culture; he submitted memorials earnestly declining and again memorials requesting dismissal—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and grand academician of the Hall of Splendid Culture. He memorialized earnestly to decline and then again to resign. Both pleas were refused.

sentences.zh: 明年三月卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following March, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨，哭之慟，廢朝三日，贈太尉、中書令，諡文簡。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person, wept bitterly, suspended court for three days, posthumously granted him Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, and gave the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person and wept bitterly. Court was suspended for three days. Minzhong was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenjian, "Cultured and Unassuming."

sentences.zh: 五子、諸婿並遷官，親校又官數人。

translations.literal: His five sons and all sons-in-law were all promoted in office; several relatives and attendants also received posts.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons and every son-in-law were promoted in rank, and several kinsmen and household attendants received offices as well.

sentences.zh: 敏中姿表瑰碩，有儀矩，性端厚愷悌，多智，曉民政，善處繁劇，慎於采拔。

translations.literal: Minzhong's bearing was magnificent and imposing, with proper decorum; his nature was upright, generous, and kind, rich in wisdom, versed in the people's affairs, skilled at handling complicated and pressing matters, and cautious in selection and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong was imposing in person and precise in bearing. He was upright, generous, and good-natured, shrewd in counsel, well versed in civilian administration, adept at tangled and urgent business, and careful in choosing men for office.

sentences.zh: 居大任三十年，時以重德目之，為人主所優禮，故雖衰疾，終不得謝。

translations.literal: For thirty years he held great office; people of the time regarded him for his profound virtue, and the sovereign treated him with special favor—so though aged and ill, he never obtained leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years he held high office, and the age looked to him for great moral weight; the emperor treated him with exceptional honor, so that even when he was worn out and sick he could never win permission to step down.

sentences.zh: 及追命制入，帝特批曰：「敏中淳謹溫良，宜益此意。」

translations.literal: When the follow-up appointment edict arrived, the emperor personally wrote on it: "Minzhong is sincere, cautious, gentle, and good—he should be guided all the more in this spirit."
translations.idiomatic: When the renewed appointment edict reached him, the emperor personally annotated it: "Minzhong is sincere, careful, gentle, and good—let him hold all the more to that spirit."

sentences.zh: 其恩顧如此。

translations.literal: Such was the imperial favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the throne's regard for him.

sentences.zh: 有文集十五卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works in fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of writings in fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子:傳正，國子博士；

translations.literal: Sons: Chuanzheng, Erudite of the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Chuanzheng, Erudite of the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 傳式，龍圖閣直學士；

translations.literal: Chuanshi, Hanlin Associate Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi, Hanlin Associate Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall;

sentences.zh: 傳亮，駕部員外郎；

translations.literal: Chuanliang, Outer Department Director in the Department of Carriages;
translations.idiomatic: Chuanliang, Outer Department Director in the Department of Carriages;

sentences.zh: 傳師，殿中丞；

translations.literal: Chuanshi, Palace Aide;
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi, Palace Aide;

sentences.zh: 傳範，娶南陽郡王惟吉女安福縣主，為密州觀察使，諡惠節。

translations.literal: Chuanfan, who married the Princess of Anfu, daughter of the Prince of Nanyang Wei Ji, served as observation commissioner of Mizhou, and posthumously received the title Prudent Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanfan married the Princess of Anfu, daughter of the Prince of Nanyang Wei Ji, served as observation commissioner of Mizhou, and was posthumously titled Prudent Integrity.

sentences.zh: 傳亮子經，定國軍留後，諡康懿。

translations.literal: Chuanliang's son Jing was military prefect of Dingguo Army and posthumously received the title Peaceful and Dignified.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanliang's son Jing was military prefect of Dingguo Army and was posthumously titled Peaceful and Dignified.

sentences.zh: 經女即欽聖憲肅皇后也，以后族贈敏中燕王、傳亮周王、經吳王。

translations.literal: Jing's daughter was Empress Qinsheng Xiansu; by virtue of her empress lineage Minzhong was posthumously ennobled Prince of Yan, Chuanliang Prince of Zhou, and Jing Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's daughter became Empress Qinsheng Xiansu; through her empress kinship Minzhong was posthumously made Prince of Yan, Chuanliang Prince of Zhou, and Jing Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 敏中餘孫繹、絳，並官太子中書。

translations.literal: Minzhong's remaining grandsons Yi and Jiang both held posts as secretaries in the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong's other grandsons Yi and Jiang both served as secretaries in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋至真宗之世，號為盛治，而得人亦多。

translations.literal: Commentary: By the reign of Zhenzong the Song was called an age of flourishing governance, and worthy men were indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: By Zhenzong's reign the Song was hailed as an age of good government, and men of talent were indeed plentiful.

sentences.zh: 李沆為相，正大光明，其焚封妃之詔以格人主之私，請遷靈州之民以奪西夏之謀，無愧宰相之任矣。

translations.literal: As chief councilor Li Hang was upright and open-hearted: he burned the edict to ennoble a consort and so checked the sovereign's private impulses; he urged relocating the people of Lingzhou and so foiled Western Xia's design—fully worthy of a chancellor's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang as chief councilor was upright and clear-sighted: he burned the edict to elevate a consort and checked the emperor's private desires; he urged evacuating the people of Lingzhou and blunted Western Xia's designs—no unworthy bearer of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 沆嘗謂王旦，邊患既息，人主侈心必生，而聲色、土木、神仙祠禱之事將作，後王欽若、丁謂之徒果售其佞。

translations.literal: Hang once told Wang Dan that once frontier troubles had ceased, the sovereign's appetite for extravagance would surely grow, and matters of music and women, construction, and spirit shrines with prayer would follow—and later Wang Qinruo, Ding Wei, and their like indeed peddled their flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Hang once told Wang Dan that once the frontier was quiet, the emperor's taste for extravagance would surely awaken, and music and women, building projects, and spirit shrines with prayer would follow—and later Wang Qinruo, Ding Wei, and men like them indeed sold their flattery.

sentences.zh: 又告真宗不可用新進喜事之人，中外所陳利害皆報罷之，後神宗信用安石變更之言，馴至棼擾。

translations.literal: He also warned Zhenzong against employing newly advanced men eager for novelty, and rejected every proposal of benefit and harm reported from within and without; later Shenzong trusted Wang Anshi's talk of reform, and disorder followed little by little.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Zhenzong not to employ shallow newcomers hungry for novelty, and rejected every proposal of benefit and harm reported from within and without the court; later Shenzong put his faith in Wang Anshi's talk of change, and step by step the realm fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 世稱沆為「聖相」，其言雖過，誠有先知者乎！

translations.literal: The age called Hang the "sage chief councilor"—though that goes too far, was there not something prophetic in his words?
translations.idiomatic: The age called Hang the "sage chief councilor"—the praise is excessive, yet was there not something prophetic in what he said?

sentences.zh: 王旦當國最久，事至不膠，有謗不校，薦賢而不市恩，救罪輒宥而不費辭。

translations.literal: Wang Dan directed the state longest: when affairs came before him he did not grow rigid; faced with slander he did not dispute it; he recommended the worthy without trading in favors; when interceding for the guilty he pardoned them without wasted words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan held the reins of government longest: when business came before him he did not stiffen; when slandered he did not answer back; he recommended the worthy without trading in gratitude; when he pleaded for the guilty he pardoned them without a word wasted.

sentences.zh: 澶淵之役，請於真宗曰：「十日不捷，何以處之？」

translations.literal: In the Chanyuan campaign he asked Zhenzong: "If there is no victory within ten days, how are we to proceed?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Chanyuan campaign he asked Zhenzong, "If no victory comes within ten days, what then are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 真宗答之曰：「立太子。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong answered: "Install the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong answered, "Install the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 契丹逾歲給而借幣，西夏告民饑而假糧，皆一語定之，偉哉宰相才也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan asked beyond their annual tribute to borrow coin and silk, and Western Xia reported that its people were starving and requested grain on loan—all were settled with a single remark. What chancellor's talent!
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan asked beyond their annual tribute quota to borrow coin and silk, and Western Xia reported that its people were starving and requested grain on loan—each was settled with a single remark. What chancellor's gift!

sentences.zh: 惟受王欽若之說，以遂天書之妄，斯則不及李沆爾。

translations.literal: Only in accepting Wang Qinruo's counsel and thus completing the folly of the Heavenly Writings did he fall short of Li Hang.
translations.idiomatic: Only in accepting Wang Qinruo's counsel and carrying through the folly of the Heavenly Writings did he fall short of Li Hang.

sentences.zh: 向敏中恥受贓物之賜以遠其汙，預避市舶之嫌以全其廉，堅拒皇甫侃之書以免其累，拜罷之際，喜慍不形，亦可謂有宰相之風焉。

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong was ashamed to accept gifts of illicit goods and so kept clear of taint; he foresaw the suspicion attached to the maritime trade commission and so preserved his integrity; he firmly refused Huangfu Kan's letters and so escaped entanglement; at investiture and dismissal alike joy and anger never showed on his face—he too may be said to have had a chancellor's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong was ashamed to take gifts of tainted goods and kept himself clear of stain; he avoided in advance the suspicion that clung to the maritime trade commission and preserved his integrity whole; he firmly refused Huangfu Kan's letters and so escaped being implicated; at appointment and removal alike neither joy nor anger showed on his face—he too may be said to have borne a chancellor's manner.
